item.title: England 'not thinking about points difference' against France
item.description: England hooker Brad O'Neill says his side will resist the urge to go for broke when they face France in their second Rugby League World Cup match in Perth on Saturday.

item.title: NFL Survivor contest picks, predictions, advice, strategy: My favorite Week 7 selections
item.description: Normally, when there’s Survivor blood in the streets of Los Angeles it’s because the Chargers have done it again. In Week 7, though, the Rams were the culprits, becoming the biggest favorite to lose outright all season. Plus, what feels even less likely than a 13-point/Super Bowl favorite getting tripped up? The Tennessee Titans actually won a game. Those two stunners cut the remaining pool entrants by more than half once again, and just 5% of the original entrants remain in Circa Sports’ massive Survivor contest after just six weeks: Week 6 results from the Circa NFL Survivor Contest. While that percentage should roughly mirror the number remaining in your pool, how many entrants remain changes the calculus when it comes to strategy. After all, the fewer the entrants, the less conceptual risk is necessary each week. Most likely path To get to this point, we can get pretty close to narrowing down the most likely path for survival, all of which have been options in our weekly Survivor contest outlook: Week 1: Jaguars (over Browns)/Steelers (over Falcons) Week 2: 49ers (over Cardinals) Week 3: Chiefs (over Dolphins) Week 4: Vikings (over Dolphins)/Ravens (over Titans) Week 5: Texans (over Titans)/Jaguars (over Eagles) Week 6: Patriots (over Jets) This provides context in understanding that it matters who you’ve already taken, and what you might be giving up by burning a team that week. Week 7 moneylines How likely is a team to win and you'll advance? The betting market provides the answer to that each week with the moneyline, which we can convert to an implied win probability. The favorite, moneyline and implied win percentage for every favorite in Week 7. Market power ratings It's not as simple as picking the team most likely to win, because once you use that team, you can't use it again. What is simple is that if you're going to make it through the 18-week season, then you need to use 18 teams. Week 7 moneylines How likely is a team to win and you'll advance? The betting market provides the answer to that each week with the moneyline, which we can convert to an implied win probability. The favorite, moneyline and implied win percentage for every favorite in Week 7. Market power ratings It's not as simple as picking the team most likely to win, because once you use that team, you can't use it again. What is simple is that if you're going to make it through the 18-week season, then you need to use 18 teams. That means, at some point, you'll be trusting the 18th-best team in the NFL — an unnerving thought. Here's a list of the current top 18 teams (with help from the betting market), and an estimation of their value to the point spread: Bills: 18.6 Rams: 18.1 Seahawks: 18.1 Chiefs: 17.6 Jaguars: 17.6 49ers: 17.6 Ravens: 17.6 Bears: 17.3 Texans: 16.7 Bengals: 16.5 Patriots: 16.2 Lions: 15.9 Vikings: 15.1 Broncos: 14.6 Cowboys: 14.3 Panthers: 14.3 Steelers: 14.3 Packers: 13.5 Picking the most likely team to win each week, or the highest available team on this list above, means that you're giving up the opportunity to use it later, and while every week is technically created equal, trusting a team in September is nerve-wracking, but doing so at some point in December is real tension. Week 7’s Survivor pick Now that we have a good understanding of how the survivors have made it through Week 6, we’re down to “one-and-done” for our pick, and the decision tree that will sprout from that selection. Once we’re out, we’re out. The implied probability derived from the moneyline should answer any questions about why the favorite should win, but the nuance is found in what you’re giving up by using them now and not later (with a projected point spread projection for those matchups). Texans (80.9%) over Giants Survivor combines skill and luck like no other betting-related vehicle. Skill: Turning away from the Jaguars in Week 1, using another team to get by, saving Jacksonville for a later date. Luck: Using the Jaguars in Week 5 against the Eagles, and getting bailed out in the final seconds of that game. That combination is the most likely reason as to why Circa’s “availability matrix” has Houston available for just over half (52.5%) of remaining contestants. Whether it’s Jameis Winston or J.J. McCarthy starting at quarterback for the Giants, this is the time to take Houston, with back-to-back wins under their belt, as the biggest favorite of the week. Estimated Availability: 52.5% What you’re giving up (projected point spread) : Week 9 at Chargers (HOU -4.5) Week 11 vs. Colts (HOU -7.5) Week 18 vs. Titans (HOU -11) We’d love to keep the Texans holstered, allowing others to take them, and have Houston as a trump card later on, but the other options this week are too sketchy to want to use. Are you one of the 47.5% of Survivor contestants to have burned the Texans in Week 5? Hopefully, you’re in the 58.3% cohort who still has available the second-biggest favorite — the Vikings (having likely used the Ravens in Week 4). Without access to either, you’ve likely fallen victim to poor planning, and now it’s time to roll the dice with the Jets, or test your acumen in picking a game that’s uncomfortably close to a 50/50 bet on the moneyline. Do you feel lucky with a Los Angeles team? The Cowboys? The Steelers in Paris? Well, do ya? You can find more valuable betting analysis from Yahoo Sports betting contributor, Matt Russell , at THE WINDOW .

item.title: Apple Music has a new logo
item.description: Apple is officially launching a rebrand of Apple Music. Following the appearance of a redesigned wordmark in a video and an updated app icon in an iOS 27.2 beta , Apple introduced the new "identity" for Apple Music today . There's a new logo, the updated wordmark, and a new sound composed by British producer Fred Again and Nest Acoustics. In a video , Apple says that for the rebrand, the company "wanted sound to create the visuals," showing the music note logo and the wordmark underwater and how that water responded to sound. It's a pretty cool video, honestly, and I like seeing how the water morphs the logo and wordmark. The video is also one … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: Milwaukee Brewers broadcaster sends emotional message about Freddy Peralta ahead of World Series
item.description: The Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays are preparing to face off in the 2026 World Series, with several compelling storylines surrounding the matchup. Both franchises are pursuing their first championship, adding extra significance to the series. Another major subplot involves Freddy Peralta, who will face the team he spent the first eight seasons of his MLB career with. The Brewers traded Freddy Peralta to the New York Mets last offseason, but his stint in New York proved difficult as his pitching results fell short and the team struggled. The Mets later sent him to Tampa Bay, where he found his rhythm again and emerged as an important part of the Rays’ journey to the World Series. " #Brewers fans will always love Freddy. I will always love Freddy Peralta, he's one of my favorite human beings ever – but I want to beat him and the Brewers want to beat him bad…." – @JLevering4 on @JenGabeChewy *chills* pic.twitter.com/T0ymRdOxai — ESPN Milwaukee (@ESPNMilwaukee) October 20, 2026 Milwaukee broadcaster Jeff Levering recently shared his thoughts on the Brewers’ upcoming World Series matchup against their former teammate Freddy Peralta. “He will get a nice ovation,” the broadcaster remarked. “I mean, the Brewers lit him up when he was a Met this year, right before the trade deadline. It was not good, but he is a different cat now. I mean, he got into the Tampa Bay lab and he looks like Brewers Freddy Peralta. I think he’s gonna get a really good ovation… Brewers fans love Freddy, they will always love Freddy and I will always love Freddy Peralta” Freddy Peralta’s time with the Brewers Aug 5, 2025; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Brewers starting pitcher Freddy Peralta (51) reacts after giving up a home run against the Atlanta Braves in the fourth inning at Truist Park. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Peralta spent eight seasons with Milwaukee from 2018 through 2025, earning two All Star nods during his tenure. He also turned in a strong campaign in 2025, finishing fifth in the National League Cy Young Award voting. “He’s one of my favorite human beings ever, but I want to beat him. I want to beat him and the Brewers want to beat him bad,” Levering added. Aug 29, 2025; Toronto, Ontario, CAN; Brewers starting pitcher Freddy Peralta (51) delivers a pitch against the Toronto Blue Jays in the first inning at Rogers Centre. Mandatory Credit: Dan Hamilton-Imagn Images Peralta did not choose to leave Milwaukee, as the Brewers traded him to the Mets before he eventually joined Tampa Bay. Despite his departure, fans continue to value his contributions to the franchise. As Jeff Levering noted, Milwaukee will always hold a special place for Peralta, but the Brewers must now set those emotions aside and focus on beating their former teammate and the Rays in the World Series. More Brewers news from Wisconsin Sports Heroics Oct 15, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Brewers players celebrate winning the NLCS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs against the Los Angeles Dod

item.title: Sony Rolls Out New Official PS5 Update After Major Hack
item.description: The digital arms race between Sony and PlayStation hackers continues. Shortly after the PlayStation 5 homebrew community found a way to jailbreak the console's latest firmware , Sony released a new PS5 update that will likely reset this progress.
item.dc:creator: Elijah Gonzalez

item.title: OpenBSD 8.0 beefs up virtual machines and gets a taste of Wine
item.description: OpenBSD 8.0 brings bigger virtual machines, graphics improvements, and another helping of AI mockery. The round version number doesn't signal a radical break with its predecessors. OpenBSD 8.0 is the 61st release of the project. Developer Bryan Steele posted a highlights rundown on Mastodon. Wireless improvements include updates to the qwx driver for Qualcomm Wi-Fi 6 hardware. Its VMM/VMD hypervisor now supports multiprocessor VMs with up to 64 virtual CPUs in each guest. The kernel virtual memory address space on x86-64 is now 512 GB, up from 4 GB, allowing for GPUs with large amounts of VRAM. On Arm64 machines, OpenBSD supports hibernation, and on both x86-64 and Arm64 it can use CPU AES instructions for faster encrypted swap. Component upgrades include OpenSSH 10.6 and LibreSSL 4.4.0, and the DRM graphics driver stack from Linux 6.18. The default C compiler is Clang/LLVM 22, including for the SPARC64 edition – but at the cost of dropping support for the Loongson architecture. The list of errata is short, with just four fixes – but then, version 8.0 is very new. Just days before this release, there was a high-profile OpenBSD issue: Calif's "Big Fish" research describes a decades-old shared-memory bug chained with a separate kernel flaw to gain local root access. Both were fixed in OpenBSD 7.9 , through errata 026 and 018 respectively. Project leader Theo de Raadt forked OpenBSD from NetBSD 1.0 in 1995, and the first release of the new OS was OpenBSD 1.2 in July 1996 – so version 8.0 is as close as the project will get to a 30th anniversary release. According to Calif's proof-of-concept code on GitHub , the bug was in the original code that both OpenBSD and NetBSD inherited from the original BSD codebase – which is how come there's a 37-year-old bug in a 30-year-old project. A HackerNews comment says: "Interestingly, looks like this was accidentally fixed in NetBSD during a rewrite of that code in August of 1999." The project has not updated its infamous slogan. The homepage still proclaims: "Only two remote holes in the default install, in a heck of a long time!" As we noted in May when OpenBSD 7.9 appeared , the project rejects code generated by LLMs, although on the basis of licensing concerns rather than its cousin NetBSD's explicit anti-AI stance . As we reported recently , this strict anti-AI stance seems to be serving NetBSD well. OpenBSD is also an anti-AI project, and for this release, the website goes out of its way to make that very clear. OpenBSD's mascot is a pufferfish, and in the banner artwork for the new release, "Puffy" has an extra eye – and the signpost in the image's background also has malformed text, a hallmark of early image-generation bots. The eyes are also constantly blinking – one at a time – to emphasize that this is a reference to Blinky the mutant fish from The Simpsons. In case you missed The Simpsons reference, the version 8.0 release theme song makes it even more explicit: it's titled "The Simps on AI." The lyri
item.dc:creator: Liam Proven
item.content:encoded: OpenBSD 8.0 brings bigger virtual machines, graphics improvements, and another helping of AI mockery. The round version number doesn't signal a radical break with its predecessors. OpenBSD 8.0 is the 61st release of the project. Developer Bryan Steele posted a highlights rundown on Mastodon. Wireless improvements include updates to the qwx driver for Qualcomm Wi-Fi 6 hardware. Its VMM/VMD hypervisor now supports multiprocessor VMs with up to 64 virtual CPUs in each guest. The kernel virtual memory address space on x86-64 is now 512 GB, up from 4 GB, allowing for GPUs with large amounts of VRAM. On Arm64 machines, OpenBSD supports hibernation, and on both x86-64 and Arm64 it can use CPU AES instructions for faster encrypted swap. Component upgrades include OpenSSH 10.6 and LibreSSL 4.4.0, and the DRM graphics driver stack from Linux 6.18. The default C compiler is Clang/LLVM 22, including for the SPARC64 edition – but at the cost of dropping support for the Loongson architecture. The list of errata is short, with just four fixes – but then, version 8.0 is very new. Just days before this release, there was a high-profile OpenBSD issue: Calif's "Big Fish" research describes a decades-old shared-memory bug chained with a separate kernel flaw to gain local root access. Both were fixed in OpenBSD 7.9 , through errata 026 and 018 respectively. Project leader Theo de Raadt forked OpenBSD from NetBSD 1.0 in 1995, and the first release of the new OS was OpenBSD 1.2 in July 1996 – so version 8.0 is as close as the project will get to a 30th anniversary release. According to Calif's proof-of-concept code on GitHub , the bug was in the original code that both OpenBSD and NetBSD inherited from the original BSD codebase – which is how come there's a 37-year-old bug in a 30-year-old project. A HackerNews comment says: "Interestingly, looks like this was accidentally fixed in NetBSD during a rewrite of that code in August of 1999." The project has not updated its infamous slogan. The homepage still proclaims: "Only two remote holes in the default install, in a heck of a long time!" As we noted in May when OpenBSD 7.9 appeared , the project rejects code generated by LLMs, although on the basis of licensing concerns rather than its cousin NetBSD's explicit anti-AI stance . As we reported recently , this strict anti-AI stance seems to be serving NetBSD well. OpenBSD is also an anti-AI project, and for this release, the website goes out of its way to make that very clear. OpenBSD's mascot is a pufferfish, and in the banner artwork for the new release, "Puffy" has an extra eye – and the signpost in the image's background also has malformed text, a hallmark of early image-generation bots. The eyes are also constantly blinking – one at a time – to emphasize that this is a reference to Blinky the mutant fish from The Simpsons. In case you missed The Simpsons reference, the version 8.0 release theme song makes it even more explicit: it's titled "The Simps on AI." The lyrics and the vocals parody both Simpsons characters and AI users. Our favorite line sounds like Grampa Simpson, and says: Back in my day we didn't have artificial intelligence, we had real stupidity – and we liked it. We've seen negative reactions online, but then we often find that some people lack much of a sense of humor. For our part, we really enjoyed seeing the OpenBSD team having such fun. We reckon it will appeal to many Butlerian Jihadi types. It certainly did to The Reg FOSS desk. A little Wine with your pufferfish A couple of days before the 8.0 release came an unexpected announcement on the openbsd-ports mailing list: a proposed port of Wine for OpenBSD . This is a new version of the Wine 11 runtime that allows Windows binaries to launch and run on OpenBSD. This is a 64-bit version of Wine for OpenBSD on x86-64, and for now, this means it can only run 64-bit Windows code. (For the technical nitty-gritty: Wine needs to manipulate the CPU's GS register. Windows on x86-64 uses the GS segment base to locate the Thread Environment Block (TEB), as the late great Geoff Chappell explained . This is a very longstanding Windows data structure, going all the way back through Windows 95 to OS/2 . The port was particularly tricky because OpenBSD doesn't allow programs to alter that, so the port is emulating instructions that use the %gs segment override. The snags are that this means 32-bit code doesn't work, and secondly, because this is unnecessary on Linux, the code is unlikely to be merged back into upstream Wine.) If you want to see it working, there are a few screenshot galleries on Reddit's openbsd_gaming group, showing a number of recent major titles running: Some samples from WIP wine port , more wine-on-OpenBSD screenshots , and even more wine-on-OpenBSD proof . The port comes hedged with caveats, notable among them that Wine does not do any kind of sandboxing, so using it potentially opens up OpenBSD to Windows malware. However, for some users, this could be a very useful addition. OpenBSD is the simplest and cleanest member of the BSD family, indeed, of the FOSS Unix family. Part of this is because entire subsystems are missing that the other BSDs provide. Bluetooth connections to Apple's wireless keyboards and pointing devices aren't supported. There's no logical volume management – which would massively help with OpenBSD's complex disk partitioning. There's no journaling filesystem either (although a port of the new Gefs is in progress ). While small and clean, its priorities favor security and simplicity, though performance will depend on the hardware and workload. Importantly – since you probably will need to ask for help – the OpenBSD community does not have a reputation for friendliness. Saying that, it is quite a lot easier to get OpenBSD installed and running, complete with its 25-year-old version 2.2.5 of the Fvwm window manager , than either NetBSD or FreeBSD. If you're looking for an AI-free, and indeed systemd-free, path away from Linux, OpenBSD 8.0 is very definitely worth a try. ®

item.title: Three Como players who can make an impact v Manchester United
item.description: Three Como players who can make an impact v Manchester United Serie A side Como play a historic Champions League tie against Manchester United today. While there have been fears that the tie could be postponed, it is set to go ahead, with the Red Devils set to face a huge challenge as well. Cesc Fabregas’ side play a fluid brand of football, where they constantly exchange positions rapidly, which allows them to build from the back smoothly and transition from midfield to attack swiftly. More than the system, it is specific players that will be key for Como. Apart from the obvious names, here are three players who could be huge today. Jacobo Ramon At just 21, Jacobo Ramon has become one of the best centre-backs in Serie A. He impresses with his ability on the ball, having fulfilled the promise that was seen during his early days at Real Madrid. The talent is a perfect fit for the setup, which brings the most out of him, also allowing him to sometimes step into midfield. While not a Spain international yet, Ramon’s time could indeed soon come. Max Perrone The ex-Manchester City player is one of the most silent impact players in the Como side. He uses his left foot to dictate the tempo of games at will, breaking it up when needed too. He plays a big role in allowing Como to build up efficiently, dropping into the backline when needed and also sometimes drifting wide for the same purpose. He generally doesn’t get enough plaudits either but a big game against Manchester United could the right time for him to get the credit he deserves. Martin Baturina A much more prominent name due to his heroics in the last few months, Martin Baturina has been more important for Como than Nico Paz since 2026 started. His importance grew after a slow start and he is constantly among the goals. The Croatian floats around in attack, picking up the ball in the right spaces as he roams from one flank to the other and has a hammer of a right foot. When Baturina gets the ball, it feels like everything slows down before the takes an action. He has deceptive 1v1 ability too, which can be a big threat for Manchester United. Kaustubh Pandey – GIFN

item.title: How much money does Gianni Infantino make at FIFA? Breaking down president's salary after reports of secret payments
item.description: How much money does Gianni Infantino make at FIFA? Breaking down president's salary after reports of secret payments originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Ever since the conclusion of the 2026 FIFA World Cup this past summer, the heat has been on Gianni Infantino's position as FIFA president. The whirlwind began when Infantino was caught attempting to sell shares of the World Cup to private equity investors, which sent fans and fellow executives into a frenzy. This scandal resulted in Infantino's position being called into question, and created a tense atmosphere in the lead-up to the upcoming FIFA presidential elections to come next spring. Now, Infantino has once again been placed in the spotlight after he was reportedly found being paid extra compensation in addition to what FIFA disclosed publicly in its 2026 annual report, leading questions as to what else he could be receiving out of the public eye. MORE: Ranking the top candidates for the 2026 Ballon d'Or Gianni Infantino salary as FIFA president FIFA has committed to publishing president Gianni Infantino's salary each year in its annual report, declaring his compensation in the company's yearly release. For the 2025 calendar year, Infantino was paid 4.8 million Swiss Francs (CHF), or $5.76 million in gross salary, according to FIFA's annual compensation report . This is broken down into 2.6 million CHF in base salary, and 2.2 million CHF in bonuses. Report claims Gianni Infantino paid undisclosed salary According to a report by Martyn Ziegler of The Times , who also broke the story about FIFA's attempts to sell World Cup shares last month, Gianni Infantino was paid additionally on top of his disclosed salary by FIFA. The report cites 2024 U.S. tax filings by FIFA which show that Infantino was given $1.76 million by FWC2026, the company FIFA set up to run the 2026 FIFA World Cup in the United States this past summer. U.S.-based non-profits must fill out IRS form 990, on which FIFA disclosed to the U.S. government payments by FWC2026 to Infantino as well as FIFA General Secretary Matias Graffstrom, CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani, and a number of other executives involved in the tournament's production. This salary came on top of his regularly reported compensation, and was not publicly disclosed in FIFA's financial filings in their annual report. They also acknowledged that claims regarding a Miami property purchase were false.
item.content:encoded: How much money does Gianni Infantino make at FIFA? Breaking down president's salary after reports of secret payments originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Ever since the conclusion of the 2026 FIFA World Cup this past summer, the heat has been on Gianni Infantino's position as FIFA president. The whirlwind began when Infantino was caught attempting to sell shares of the World Cup to private equity investors, which sent fans and fellow executives into a frenzy. This scandal resulted in Infantino's position being called into question, and created a tense atmosphere in the lead-up to the upcoming FIFA presidential elections to come next spring. Now, Infantino has once again been placed in the spotlight after he was reportedly found being paid extra compensation in addition to what FIFA disclosed publicly in its 2026 annual report, leading questions as to what else he could be receiving out of the public eye. MORE: Ranking the top candidates for the 2026 Ballon d'Or Gianni Infantino salary as FIFA president FIFA has committed to publishing president Gianni Infantino's salary each year in its annual report, declaring his compensation in the company's yearly release. For the 2025 calendar year, Infantino was paid 4.8 million Swiss Francs (CHF), or $5.76 million in gross salary, according to FIFA's annual compensation report . This is broken down into 2.6 million CHF in base salary, and 2.2 million CHF in bonuses. Report claims Gianni Infantino paid undisclosed salary According to a report by Martyn Ziegler of The Times , who also broke the story about FIFA's attempts to sell World Cup shares last month, Gianni Infantino was paid additionally on top of his disclosed salary by FIFA. The report cites 2024 U.S. tax filings by FIFA which show that Infantino was given $1.76 million by FWC2026, the company FIFA set up to run the 2026 FIFA World Cup in the United States this past summer. U.S.-based non-profits must fill out IRS form 990, on which FIFA disclosed to the U.S. government payments by FWC2026 to Infantino as well as FIFA General Secretary Matias Graffstrom, CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani, and a number of other executives involved in the tournament's production. This salary came on top of his regularly reported compensation, and was not publicly disclosed in FIFA's financial filings in their annual report. However, this report was officially retracted on October 20 by The Times who conceded that FIFA's report did not disclose this additional income because Swiss reporting rules do not count expense and reimbursement payments as compensation. They also acknowledged that claims regarding a Miami property purchase were false.

item.title: Anderson, 44, not offered new Lancashire contract
item.description: James Anderson is England's all-time leading Test wicket-taker with 704 dismissals [Getty Images] James Anderson's legendary career could be over after Lancashire opted against offering England's all-time leading wicket-taker a new contract. Anderson, 44, chose to continue playing with Lancashire after England forced him into international retirement in 2024. He captained Lancashire in the County Championship last season but the Red Rose endured a poor campaign, finishing next to bottom of Division Two. Now, as first reported by the Times, Anderson will not be given the opportunity to play at Old Trafford in 2027 - the summer when he will turn 45. It is not known whether Anderson will retire or look to extend his 26-year professional career with another county. Anderson first played top-level cricket as a 17-year-old for Lancashire Cricket Board in 2000, then made his Lancashire debut the following year. His exit from the Red Rose comes at a time of upheaval at Old Trafford. The county are undergoing a review of their cricket operations, led by interim chair Dame Sarah Storey and new chief executive Richard Kenyon. Paul Farbrace was appointed as Lancashire's director of cricket earlier this month. Although Anderson is in his mid-40s, he has remained in supreme form in a struggling team. He took 50 wickets in the County Championship in 2026, a tally bettered by only six other bowlers in Division Two. Anderson was named Lancashire's Championship player of the year. Overall, 443 of Anderson's 1,193 first-class wickets came for Lancashire, to go with 83 List A wickets and 50 T20 wickets for the county. In a 23-year international career, Anderson took 991 wickets across formats for England. Only spinners Muttiah Muralitharan of Sri Lanka and Australia's Shane Warne have more in international cricket. In 2024, Anderson became the third bowler in Test history, after Muralitharan and Warne, to reach 700 wickets. He remains third on the all-time list with 704, a record for a pace bowler that is unlikely to be broken. Later that year, Anderson was asked to call time on his international career by England's then hierarchy of coach Brendon McCullum, captain Ben Stokes and director of cricket Rob Key. He played his 188th and final Test against West Indies at Lord's before embarking on a short spell as England's bowling consultant. In 2025, Anderson signed a new deal with Lancashire and suggested he could play county cricket for three more seasons. In April of that year, he was knighted for services to cricket. Anderson stood in as Lancashire captain during the 2025 season and was given the job full-time for 2026. He was understood to be enjoying the role and, at the end of the this summer, there was no suggestion Anderson would end his career. On Wednesday, as reports of his exit from Old Trafford began to emerge, those close to Anderson were unaware of the situation. Lancashire have not commented. Essex sign wicketkeeper Bell from Lancashire Farbrace leaves

item.title: Former Open champion Oosthuizen quits LIV Golf
item.description: Louis Oosthuizen has 11 victories on the DP World Tour [Getty Images] Former Open Championship winner Louis Oosthuizen has become the latest high-profile player to quit LIV Golf, describing it as the "hardest decision he has had to make in his career". The league filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the United States in September after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund withdrew its multibillion-dollar backing. Oosthuizen, 44, joined LIV Golf in 2022 and was captain of the Southern Guards GC team. The South African now plans to return to the DP World Tour in 2027. "Five years ago, I made one of the best decisions of my life, moving away from the traditional golf world and into something very special with LIV Golf and Southern Guards GC," Oosthuizen posted on social media. "I'm the biggest supporter of team golf and always will be. Golf needs more of it. "This is probably the hardest decision I've had to make in my career, but I have to do what I believe is right for my golf." The 2010 Open champion, who has finished as a runner-up at least once in each of the other three majors, said a more flexible playing schedule will help him to compete at a high level. "I realised I have a lot more in me, and my biggest fear was that the schedule on LIV 2.0 would be tough to manage," said former world number four Oosthuizen. "I feel I have a few more years of good, competitive golf left in me, and the only way to be really sharp and competitive is through a schedule I control." Oosthuizen joins Thomas Pieters, Sergio Garcia, Abraham Ancer, David Puig and Adrian Meronk in announcing his departure. Last week, two-time major winner Jon Rahm gave up a reported £75m owed to him by LIV Golf after reaching a separation agreement. Some former LIV Golf players, including Brooks Koepka, have since rejoined the PGA Tour, which rewrote its rules in December to allow the five-time major winner to return, subject to certain sanctions. Guy Kinnings, CEO of the DP World Tour, told BBC Sport earlier this month that players who continue with LIV will not be allowed to be members of the European tour next season. LIV has secured a possible $300m (£224.2m) in financing from BC Partners Credit in order to try to move forward with the 2027 season.

item.title: Former Vanderbilt QB lands new career opportunity
item.description: Former Vanderbilt QB lands new career opportunity originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Former Vanderbilt Commodores quarterback Diego Pavia is taking the next step in his professional career. He is in negotiations with the United Football League (UFL), he announced Tuesday in a post on X. The upcoming UFL draft is set for Wednesday, November 18, in St. Louis. Players do not need to be signed to a UFL roster to be draft-eligible. When a player gets drafted, that team has the right to negotiate a deal with the potential player. appreciate everyone reaching out with everything on my career. my agent @malkikawa and the UFL are currently in negotiations to make this happen! whatever team I end up at, I can promise you one thing- You will get everything I got 💯 — Diego Pavia (@diegopavia02) October 21, 2026 Pavia went undrafted in the 2026 NFL Draft before being signed by the Ravens as an undrafted free agent (UDFA). The Ravens waived him on July 23, and he did not make the 90-man roster. At Vanderbilt, Pavia was the 2025 Heisman Trophy runner-up and led the Commodores to back-to-back winning seasons. He finished his time in Nashville with 5,832 passing yards and 49 passing touchdowns, completing 65% of his passes, and added 1,662 rushing yards and 18 rushing touchdowns. Pavia looks to prove the NFL made a mistake by not drafting him, and he's looking for another chance. item.title: Crystal Palace 'handball' goal v Forest not a VAR error - panel
item.description: [Getty Images] The Premier League's Key Match Incidents Panel says Crystal Palace's second goal against Nottingham Forest should have been disallowed on the field for handball - but backed the video assistant referee's decision not to intervene. The game was locked at 1-1 deep into first-half stoppage time when Jefferson Lerma appeared to nod the ball through the legs of Forest keeper Matz Sels. However, it soon transpired that the ball had deflected off the elbow of team-mate Anan Khalail on its way into goal. That meant the goal technically belonged to Khalail, who could not score a goal with his arm. This was not picked up in the initial replays, only becoming clear during the half-time analysis on the television coverage. Palace went on to win the game 3-1 at Selhurst Park. The Premier League's KMI Panel voted 3:2 that it was an on-field mistake by referee Peter Bankes, but it was unanimous that the VAR, Darren England, was right not to rule out the goal. "On the balance of probability the ball is likely to have come into contact with Khalaili's arm," the KMI Panel said. "The panel all supported the VAR's decision to not intervene on the basis that the footage readily available to the VAR doesn't show conclusive evidence of a handball." It will sting for Forest as they had a Neco Williams goal ruled out for handball in their 0-0 draw with Tottenham through a VAR intervention. Williams insisted after the game the ball did not touch his arm, but replays which later emerged appeared to prove it did . The KMI Panel unanimously supported the decision. Bankes was on VAR duty for the disallowed goal against Spurs.

item.title: [VIDEO] ‘This Govt Has Normalised Lack Of Empathy,’ Rhodes-Vivour Condemns Use Of Tear Gas At #EndSARS Anniversary
item.description: The candidate of the African Democratic Party (ADC) for the February 16, 2027, governorship election in Lagos State, Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour, has condemned the use of tear gas canisters during the sixth anniversary of #EndSARS at the Lekki Toll Gate. Speaking during an interview on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief on Wednesday, Rhodes-Vivour accused the All Progressives Congress-led Federal Government of normalising the lack of empathy for Nigerians who lost their lives during the October 2020 protest against police brutality. “They are normalising this bullying system of governance that has come to describe what the APC government has become, and the citizen is going to have to really understand what is at stake here because we need a government that actually understands that lives were lost on this day,” he said. “Innocent citizens were killed.” ﻿ The post [VIDEO] ‘This Govt Has Normalised Lack Of Empathy,’ Rhodes-Vivour Condemns Use Of Tear Gas At #EndSARS Anniversary appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Who will replace Mike Locksley? The top candidates Maryland should consider
item.description: Maryland has parted ways with coach Mike Locksley during his eight season with the program. Locksley's tenure included, three bowl berths and an overall record of 39-54, with the last straw Saturday’s 37-30 loss at home to fellow Big Ten afterthought Rutgers. While Locksley did have a nice run of postseason appearances from 2021-23, he was not able to capitalize on that success after the league expanded to 18 teams the following season and hit rock bottom with this year’s veteran team. His replacement will have to maximize resources that currently lag behind the best of the Big Ten. Hiring a coach with a national reputation might free up more funding and the chance to build a stronger roster. The opening will have significant draw for being in the Big Ten. But there are also significant drawbacks, namely a spotty history of winning and a difficult rebuilding job. Look for these coaches to lead the conversation: Brian Kelly The former Notre Dame and LSU coach with 200 wins in 22 seasons at the Bowl Subdivision level wants to get back into coaching but can’t afford to be picky. Maryland provides a soft landing, sort of: Kelly can get back into the Power Four and won’t face championship-or-bust expectations. Kelly also has a connection with prominent Maryland booster in Under Armour founder Kevin Plank, whose company sponsored Notre Dame. While the idea that Maryland would hire Kelly would’ve been laughed away even just two years ago, the Terrapins would be ecstatic to hire a coach with his résumé. Charles Huff, Memphis Memphis dropped to 5-2 with a loss at Tulane, but the Tigers still done pretty well in Huff’s first season, putting him on the map for lower-level Power Four openings. He’s also been a well-traveled coach who previously won consistently in short stints at Marshall and Southern Mississippi. Huff would be a solid fallback plan if Maryland is unable to hire an established Power Four coach. A bonus is Huff is a Maryland native and spent one season at the school as an assistant before stops at Penn State, Mississippi State and Alabama. Lance Taylor, Western Michigan Taylor has seen his reputation grow with Western Michigan’s MAC championship a year ago and this year’s controversial loss to Michigan. The former Stanford and Notre Dame running backs coach has steadily improved the Broncos ’ record, from 4-8 in 2023 to 6-7 and a bowl game in 2024 to 10 wins last season and a 5-2 mark just past this year’s midway point. This shows a knack for rebuilding that could be sped up by the chance to dig into the transfer portal as part of the Power Four. Zach Kittley, Florida Atlantic Even more so than Taylor, Kittley has burst onto the national scene from anonymity in the past six years. From 2020-24, he was the offensive coordinator at Houston Baptist, Western Kentucky and Texas Tech before being hired by Florida Atlantic. item.content:encoded: Maryland has parted ways with coach Mike Locksley during his eight season with the program. Locksley's tenure included, three bowl berths and an overall record of 39-54, with the last straw Saturday’s 37-30 loss at home to fellow Big Ten afterthought Rutgers. But there are also significant drawbacks, namely a spotty history of winning and a difficult rebuilding job. Look for these coaches to lead the conversation: Brian Kelly The former Notre Dame and LSU coach with 200 wins in 22 seasons at the Bowl Subdivision level wants to get back into coaching but can’t afford to be picky. Maryland provides a soft landing, sort of: Kelly can get back into the Power Four and won’t face championship-or-bust expectations. Kelly also has a connection with prominent Maryland booster in Under Armour founder Kevin Plank, whose company sponsored Notre Dame. While the idea that Maryland would hire Kelly would’ve been laughed away even just two years ago, the Terrapins would be ecstatic to hire a coach with his résumé. Charles Huff, Memphis Memphis dropped to 5-2 with a loss at Tulane, but the Tigers still done pretty well in Huff’s first season, putting him on the map for lower-level Power Four openings. He’s also been a well-traveled coach who previously won consistently in short stints at Marshall and Southern Mississippi. Huff would be a solid fallback plan if Maryland is unable to hire an established Power Four coach. A bonus is Huff is a Maryland native and spent one season at the school as an assistant before stops at Penn State, Mississippi State and Alabama. Lance Taylor, Western Michigan Taylor has seen his reputation grow with Western Michigan’s MAC championship a year ago and this year’s controversial loss to Michigan. The former Stanford and Notre Dame running backs coach has steadily improved the Broncos ’ record, from 4-8 in 2023 to 6-7 and a bowl game in 2024 to 10 wins last season and a 5-2 mark just past this year’s midway point. This shows a knack for rebuilding that could be sped up by the chance to dig into the transfer portal as part of the Power Four. Zach Kittley, Florida Atlantic Even more so than Taylor, Kittley has burst onto the national scene from anonymity in the past six years. From 2020-24, he was the offensive coordinator at Houston Baptist, Western Kentucky and Texas Tech before being hired by Florida Atlantic. After a four-win debut, this year’s team posted the best non-conference mark in program history at 3-1 and started 4-1 for the first time since 2000. While it could be one year too soon for Kittley, he’s put himself on the list for Power Four schools looking for an immediate spark on offense. Mike Shanahan and Bryan Haines, Indiana The Hoosiers’ two coordinators will be heavy targets for openings off the top tier of the Power Four. Both have played immense roles in the program’s explosive growth that fueled the school's unlikely national title run and 22-game win streak that ended against Ohio State: Shanahan has worked with Curt Cignetti to build Indiana’s explosive offense and Haines took home last year’s Broyles Award as the nation’s top assistant with his success on defense. Either would be a home-run hire for the Terrapins. Unfortunately, both could likely do better. Brian Hartline, South Florida South Florida opened 4-0 in Hartline’s first year but has since dropped two in a row, putting him under some pressure to deliver a strong second half and take advantage of the hot start. Before being hired at USF, he was seen as one of the top position coaches in the country while tutoring Ohio State’s wide receivers. This would be a gamble of a hire for Maryland, which would be betting on his potential instead of proven results and would need to roll with a learning curve. For Hartline, delivering at Maryland would bring him one step closer to getting his dream job as Ryan Day’s replacement with the Buckeyes. item.title: Why Colts are likely sellers after firing Chris Ballard before NFL trade deadline
item.description: Why Colts are likely sellers after firing Chris Ballard before NFL trade deadline originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Indianapolis Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard after the team's Week 6 loss to the Tennessee Titans . Now without a general manager, the Colts at 2-4 are heading towards the NFL trade deadline with a lot of eyes on them. Contenders around the NFL are sure to have a lot of interest in the Colts for potential mid-season acquisitions. While not everyone is going to be available for trade, there are a lot of big names who could be dealt in the coming weeks. But will this Colts team sell? ESPN's Jeremy Fowler revealed a few reasons why the Colts are likely to sell, including what NFL history suggests after Ballard's firing and the belief from teams around the NFL. Why Colts are likely trade deadline sellers in 2026 "Rival teams believe Indianapolis will be open for business ahead of the trade deadline," Fowler writes. While Carlie Irsay-Gordon's comments after Ballard's firing might indicate the team is trying to win this year, conventional wisdom suggests this Colts team should be sellers. Fowler also revealed that "it feels as if everything is on the table" for the Colts, and that could include Daniel Jones getting benched, Shane Steichen getting fired, or even a trade deadline sell-off. But after trading their first-round pick in 2027 for Sauce Gardner last trade deadline, it wouldn't be too shocking for the Colts to actually try and compete this season. However, there's reason to believe this Colts team will sell. As Fowler pointed out, the 2026 Colts situation "mirrors that of the 2025 Dolphins." That Miami Dolphins team fired GM Chris Grier before the NFL trade deadline, and they went on to be sellers. MORE : Colts fans are calling for Daniel Jones benching after ugly Titans loss While they didn't ship out every piece they had, the Dolphins did sell at the trade deadline and later continued the sell-off during the offseason. Jaylen Waddle, Jaelan Phillips, and others were traded away last year despite being key pieces of the Dolphins. This year, the Colts could follow a similar path, with players like Josh Downs, Keenan Allen, Quentin Nelson, DeForest Buckner, Grover Stewart, and maybe even Jonathan Taylor all being made available for trade. Any player not signed through the 2027 NFL season could be available for trade. If Irsay-Gordon is fine with a multi-year rebuild, then a lot of these players would make a ton of sense as trade chips this season. item.content:encoded: Why Colts are likely sellers after firing Chris Ballard before NFL trade deadline originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Indianapolis Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard after the team's Week 6 loss to the Tennessee Titans . Now without a general manager, the Colts at 2-4 are heading towards the NFL trade deadline with a lot of eyes on them. Contenders around the NFL are sure to have a lot of interest in the Colts for potential mid-season acquisitions. While not everyone is going to be available for trade, there are a lot of big names who could be dealt in the coming weeks. But will this Colts team sell? ESPN's Jeremy Fowler revealed a few reasons why the Colts are likely to sell, including what NFL history suggests after Ballard's firing and the belief from teams around the NFL. Why Colts are likely trade deadline sellers in 2026 "Rival teams believe Indianapolis will be open for business ahead of the trade deadline," Fowler writes. While Carlie Irsay-Gordon's comments after Ballard's firing might indicate the team is trying to win this year, conventional wisdom suggests this Colts team should be sellers. Fowler also revealed that "it feels as if everything is on the table" for the Colts, and that could include Daniel Jones getting benched, Shane Steichen getting fired, or even a trade deadline sell-off. But after trading their first-round pick in 2027 for Sauce Gardner last trade deadline, it wouldn't be too shocking for the Colts to actually try and compete this season. However, there's reason to believe this Colts team will sell. As Fowler pointed out, the 2026 Colts situation "mirrors that of the 2025 Dolphins." That Miami Dolphins team fired GM Chris Grier before the NFL trade deadline, and they went on to be sellers. MORE : Colts fans are calling for Daniel Jones benching after ugly Titans loss While they didn't ship out every piece they had, the Dolphins did sell at the trade deadline and later continued the sell-off during the offseason. Jaylen Waddle, Jaelan Phillips, and others were traded away last year despite being key pieces of the Dolphins. This year, the Colts could follow a similar path, with players like Josh Downs, Keenan Allen, Quentin Nelson, DeForest Buckner, Grover Stewart, and maybe even Jonathan Taylor all being made available for trade. Any player not signed through the 2027 NFL season could be available for trade. If Irsay-Gordon is fine with a multi-year rebuild, then a lot of these players would make a ton of sense as trade chips this season. With the 2025 Dolphins as a recent example of a team that fired their GM mid-season and went on to sell, and the Colts reportedly being "open for business," it appears likely that Indianapolis will be sellers at the 2026 NFL trade deadline this November. item.title: Week 7 Fantasy Football Quarterback Streamers: Kyler Murray And Tanner McKee Headline
item.description: Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray (1) warms up before the game against the Miami Dolphins at U.S. Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brad Rempel-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Week 7 is almost here, and some fantasy football owners still aren't sure who they are going to plug into their lineups at quarterback. Considering the injuries and bye weeks, that shouldn't come as a surprise. We are going to help you decide which quarterback you should start this week. These are our fantasy football quarterback streamers for Week 7. Quarterback Streamers: Week 7 QB Kyler Murray, Minnesota Vikings Murray has gotten off to a slow start to the season, but he seemed to pick it up a bit last week. In Week 6, he threw for 229 yards and a touchdown, and rushed 10 times for 51 yards. Before last week, he had rushed 10 times for 42 yards for the entire season. It seems like he could be acclimating himself to the system in Minnesota. This week he has a great matchup against the Indianapolis Colts. They have allowed the 11th-most fantasy points to quarterbacks this season and will be without their top cornerback Sauce Gardner this week. Murray and Justin Jefferson should have a field day this week against a terrible Colts defense. QB Tanner McKee, Philadelphia Eagles McKee was fine in his first start of the season last week. He wasn't spectacular, but he threw for 215 yards and a touchdown. After getting that first start under his belt, he should be even better this week in a great matchup against the Dallas Cowboys. The Cowboys are allowing the fifth-most fantasy points to quarterbacks this season. This is a game the Eagles desperately need to win. They will be playing in Philly, and their season is on the verge of a complete collapse. We will roll with McKee in a make-or-break game. If things keep going sideways, McKee could lose his job, and the coaching staff could be in danger of losing their jobs as well. QB Geno Smith, New York Jets Smith hasn't exactly been lighting the world on fire, but he hasn't been terrible, which is more than we expected from him. Last week, he threw for 252 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in a much tougher matchup against the New England Patriots. This week, he plays the Miami Dolphins, who have allowed the eighth-most fantasy points to quarterbacks this season. Smith has also been surrounded by some solid weapons. Rookies Omar Cooper Jr and Kenyon Sadiq have both flashed impressive athleticism and have proven to be solid secondary options to Garrett Wilson when called upon. item.title: Trevoh Chalobah admits regret over Chelsea exit: 'I wanted to be a legend there'
item.description: Trevoh Chalobah has said he regrets the way his Chelsea career ended, and that his ambition had been to become a “legend” at Stamford Bridge. Chelsea decided the defender was surplus to requirements in the summer and sold him to the Italian club Como for £30 million. The 27-year-old won two Club World Cups during his time with the Blues. Chalobah told The Athletic : “The team didn’t achieve what we wanted to achieve last season, but I thought I had one of my best seasons, playing the most games and scoring a few goals. “I’d been there since I was eight and I wanted to be a legend there, but sometimes the way we plan things is not how things work out. “As footballers, you’ve always got to be ready to adapt. You could be here one moment, then the next moment you’re somewhere else. Chalobah is now playing under Cesc Fabregas at Como (Getty) “But I just thought that it was the best. Chelsea means everything to me. I’m still watching the games, keeping in contact with the players and staff.” Chalobah came through the Chelsea academy, joining the club at the age of eight, and went on to make more than 150 appearances for the first team. His honours there also included an FA Cup and the Conference League. His spell in west London came to an end when Como came calling, with the club managed by Cesc Fabregas, the former Chelsea midfielder. “The manager reached out to me over the summer and explained the project and where he saw me playing,” added the England international. “I read about the rise of Como, how exciting the team is. He really wanted me and my experience. That felt good and it was time for a change. “As a footballer, it’s good to experience different things and it was an easy decision to come abroad again. The football is amazing. The manager we have is great.” Como finished fourth in Serie A last season to secure Champions League qualification for the first time. They are due to play Manchester United on Wednesday evening, with Michael Carrick’s side in desperate need of three points after a six-game winless run.

item.title: Angel Reese’s Lights Out WNBA Finals Performance Has Kelsey Plum Comparing Her to 5x MVP A’ja Wilson
item.description: Angel Reese © X/ @AtlantaDream Angel Reese has been playing lights out in her first WNBA Finals. The talented Atlanta Dream forward notched a historic double-double on Monday night, leading the Dream to a 79-65 victory over the Golden State Valkyries to tie the best-of-seven series at 1-1. Reese played 34 minutes, finishing with 30 points and 16 rebounds, becoming the youngest player in WNBA Finals history to record such a stat line. Her impact has turned heads across the basketball world, including Phoenix Mercury guard Kelsey Plum. Plum, who appeared as a guest on the “Girls Tripp” podcast on Tuesday, said Reese reminded her in some ways of her former teammate and five-time WNBA MVP A’ja Wilson because Reese rises to the occasion in big moments. “When I watched the game, the biggest thing that stood out to me, and I’m gonna take it full circle,” Plum said (9:50 onward). “A’ja Wilson has been the best player in the league for the last half a decade. Not because she’s one of the biggest players out there…The consistency, the ability to show up in big moments, carry the weight, not let it affect your performance, and deliver time in and time out is what makes her her. “And what I saw last night was Angel, after Game 1, made a decision mentally to say, ‘I’m going to perform on both sides of the ball.’ She was phenomenal defensively, making key plays throughout the entire game – whether guarding on the perimeter; obviously her rebounds speak for itself, but her blocks. Offensively, she was not deterred. Mentally, she made a decision that she was going to win that game… I think Angel won Game 2 before the game was even played.” It is easy to understand why Plum was impressed by Reese’s performance. After holding Reese scoreless in the second half of Game 1 of the WNBA Finals, Golden State had no answers for the forward in Game 2. With this win, the Dream secured their first-ever WNBA Finals victory after going 0-10 in their previous three championship appearances. Reese and the Dream will now look to build on this huge win when they meet the Valkyries in Game 3 at State Farm Arena. Kelsey Plum Questions Who on Golden State Can Match Angel Reese Mentally In the same episode of the “Girls Tripp” podcast, Kelsey Plum questioned whether the Golden State Valkyries have what it takes to go toe-to-toe with Angel Reese without the backing of their home crowd at Ballhalla. “Angel has now set the bar. Who on Golden State is going to match that? And that, to me, is the biggest question,” Plum said. “Now I’m looking at Atlanta going home. You know, they (Valkyries) don’t have Ballhalla on their side right now. Who from Golden State is going to go toe-to-toe with Angel mentally? … I don’t know who’s mentally strong enough. Not saying there isn’t, but I don’t know who’s stronger, either individually or collectively, to match that for Golden State.” Heading into Game 3, there has to be a healthy dose of desperation from the Valkyries. Winning is what matters most,

item.title: Patriots Keys to Victory vs. Bears in Week 7 NFL Game
item.description: Patriots Keys to Victory vs. Bears in Week 7 NFL Game originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Patriots are riding high once again, back to looking like an AFC playoff contender after a slow start. But they'll face a challenge in Week 7. New England will take on a red-hot Bears offense on "Thursday Night Football," a short week for Mike Vrabel's unit as it also deals with injuries on both sides of the ball, particularly on the offensive line. Chicago comes in with the same record as the Patriots, 4-2, as Caleb Williams returned from injury last week to lead his team to a win over the Falcons. Stopping Ben Johnson's offense will be tough — but a win for New England could do a lot for momentum moving forward. Here's a look at three keys for a Patriots win over the Bears on Thursday night. MORE: How Drake Maye Rediscovered His All-Pro Form Patriots Keys to Victory vs. Bears Control Chicago's ground attack Because of Williams' injury, the Bears' offense hasn't had much consistency over six games. Chicago dropped 59 points in Week 1 with Williams, but just 10 combined in Weeks 2 and 5 when he was hurt. If one thing is clear, however, it's that Johnson's offense is built around the run game. Chicago leads the NFL with 160.7 rushing yards per game as a team, allowing Williams to play a bit more freely and take some shots downfield. Against the Falcons last week, D'Andre Swift scored twice, while Roschon Johnson scored as well. The Bears have dominated time of possession in their wins (40 minutes vs. Atlanta) thanks to their ground attack. For the Patriots, it's going to be difficult to win if they can't get the Bears' offense off the field; according to NFL.com , the Bears are averaging just 50.2 defensive snaps per game, a figure lower than any team has finished with since at least 2000. The Bears' defense hasn't been asked to do much because of how long the offense has been on the field. That can't happen for New England. The Patriots have had one of the better run-stopping defenses in the league so far (91.8 rushing yards allowed per game, 9th in NFL), but they need their interior defensive line to set the tone on first and second down vs. Chicago. A.J. Brown bounce-back game? A.J. Brown has played two games as a Patriot. Neither have lived up to expectations, but it's a long NFL season. After getting hurt in his Patriots debut in Week 1, Brown returned against the Jets last week, but struggled with drops despite being targeted 10 times by Drake Maye. If New England is going to be a playoff team this year, it needs Brown at his best. And chances are, the former All-Pro will bounce back. The Patriots could use a statement game from Brown — Maye has stepped up his play in recent weeks, putting his turnover concerns in the past and using his legs more often. It's opened things up for Vrabel's offense, but if there's one aspect still missing, it's a reliable, WR1-like weapon Maye can rely on. With Romeo Doubs now out, the Patriots need Brown to showcase his star talents in Week 6. In a prime-time matchup, there's no better stage for him to have his best game of the season yet. Drake Maye beating Bears' secondary deep On a similar note, the Bears' defense is good against the pass and run, but if there's one area Maye could exploit, it's with his deep ball. In the Bears' two losses this season, they've given up some chunk plays. Against the Vikings in Week 2, Carson Wentz was at least able to sustain three field goal drives with a 30-yard completion to Justin Jefferson, a 19-yard pass to T.J. There will be moments where Maye could have a good look deep, whether it's to Brown, Kyle Williams or DeMario Douglas. Considering the Bears stop the run well, those moments will be critical. item.title: What did Dan Hurley mean by calling UConn's big men ‘Oppenheimer' after preseason win?
item.description: EAST LANSING, MICHIGAN - OCTOBER 20: Head coach Dan Hurley of the UConn Huskies reacts in the first half of the game against the Michigan State Spartans at Breslin Center on October 20, 2026 in East Lansing, Michigan. (Photo by Rey Del Rio/Getty Images) (Rey Del Rio/Getty Images) EAST LANSING, Mich. - Was Dan Hurley referring to an Oscar, or Oskar? Or maybe both. Shortly after the UConn men's basketball team's impressive, 78-70 exhibition game win over Michigan State on Tuesday night, Hurley, as most coaches do, found some negatives in the Huskies' performance. In particular, the play of UConn centers Na'jai Hines and Oskar Giltay, who combined for more fouls (nine) than rebounds (eight). "That wasn't exactly a (expletive) Oppenheimer performance," he said of his big man tandem. Hurley apologized for his profanity, saying he was hoping to get through the season without cursing during a postgame press conference. That didn't even make it to the regular season. He didn't explain what he meant by his "Oppenheimer" quote. Was he implying that Hines and Giltay hardly had Academy Award-winning performances, a la Cillian Murphy and Robert Downey Jr. in the film "Oppenheimer," which also copped a Best Picture Oscar? Or was he simply going ... um ... nuclear on his bigs. Oscar or Oskar (and Na'jai)? Clearly, he wasn't too pleased with the latter. "We've got to get our inside game going," Hurley said. "We didn't get enough post catches ... It's like our running game. We don't have it where we need it to be right now." No coach will ever come out of a game, especially an exhibition game, 100-percent pleased. Hurley's own father says he's not happy unless he's complaining about something. But even Hurley could barely contain the pleasure he took in watching his team convincingly beat the No. 6 team in the nation, in front of a full house on its home floor and without Braylon Mullins . "I was pleasantly surprised with how we held up," he confessed. EAST LANSING, MI - OCTOBER 20: UConn Huskies center Na'Jai Hines (9) reacts to a forced turnover on the defensive end of the floor during a college basketball exhibition game between the Michigan State Spartans and UConn Huskies on October 20, 2026 at the Breslin Center in East Lansing, MI. (Photo by Adam Ruff/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) (Icon Sportswire/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Indeed, Hurley seemed to be nitpicking a bit about his center's play. Hines was the best player on the floor in the Huskies' 20-point exhibition win over Syracuse a week earlier, coming off the bench for 17 points and eight rebounds. That earned him the starting spot on Tuesday night, one he's not likely to relinquish the rest of the way. He finished with eight points, three assists, two blocks and just two boards in 17 minutes before fouling out. Hines scored on a nifty, left-handed hook shot that's looking like a real weapon for the 6-foot-11 sophomore, and had a couple of monster dunks, as well. Still, it was the second ti

He didn't explain what he meant by his "Oppenheimer" quote. Was he implying that Hines and Giltay hardly had Academy Award-winning performances, a la Cillian Murphy and Robert Downey Jr. in the film "Oppenheimer," which also copped a Best Picture Oscar? Or was he simply going ... um ... nuclear on his bigs. Oscar or Oskar (and Na'jai)? Clearly, he wasn't too pleased with the latter. "We've got to get our inside game going," Hurley said. "We didn't get enough post catches ... It's like our running game. We don't have it where we need it to be right now." No coach will ever come out of a game, especially an exhibition game, 100-percent pleased. Hurley's own father says he's not happy unless he's complaining about something. But even Hurley could barely contain the pleasure he took in watching his team convincingly beat the No. 6 team in the nation, in front of a full house on its home floor and without Braylon Mullins . "I was pleasantly surprised with how we held up," he confessed. EAST LANSING, MI - OCTOBER 20: UConn Huskies center Na'Jai Hines (9) reacts to a forced turnover on the defensive end of the floor during a college basketball exhibition game between the Michigan State Spartans and UConn Huskies on October 20, 2026 at the Breslin Center in East Lansing, MI. (Photo by Adam Ruff/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) (Icon Sportswire/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Indeed, Hurley seemed to be nitpicking a bit about his center's play. Hines was the best player on the floor in the Huskies' 20-point exhibition win over Syracuse a week earlier, coming off the bench for 17 points and eight rebounds. That earned him the starting spot on Tuesday night, one he's not likely to relinquish the rest of the way. He finished with eight points, three assists, two blocks and just two boards in 17 minutes before fouling out. Hines scored on a nifty, left-handed hook shot that's looking like a real weapon for the 6-foot-11 sophomore, and had a couple of monster dunks, as well. Still, it was the second time in as many exhibitions that UConn's starting center fouled out. Giltay had fouled out of the Syracuse game with just four points and two rebounds. He played better on Tuesday, finishing with four points and six rebounds in 19 minutes. He also committed four fouls. The foul troubles of Hines and Giltay are probably the bigger worry than how many post catches they get. Less than a minute before halftime, Giltay picked up his third foul and Hurley summoned 7-foot Bosnian Elmer Dzafic from the bench. But no sooner had Dzafic got up from his seat when Hurley changed his mind and instead called for Jacob Ross to enter the game. Ross, the younger brother of Jayden, sat out last season as a redshirt and isn't expected to play much this season. He's also just 6-6, 205 pounds - not exactly your classic big. EAST LANSING, MI - OCTOBER 20: Michigan State Spartans forward Jesse McCulloch (35) swats the shot of UConn Huskies center Oskar Giltay (18) at the rim during a college basketball exhibition game between the Michigan State Spartans and UConn Huskies on October 20, 2026 at the Breslin Center in East Lansing, MI. (Photo by Adam Ruff/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) (Icon Sportswire/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Early in the latter half, Ross got a couple more minutes of run. Dzafic, a sophomore expected to be the team's third center, never got into the game. Why was that? It had less to do with a lack of faith in Dzafic and more simply a matchup situation, Hurley explained. The Spartans were playing a little small-ball with 6-9 Cam Ward at the five, and he would have been a bad match-up for Dzafic. "We're trying, to a degree, to bulk Jacob up and have him play a little positionless five," Hurley added. "Maybe utilized him in a way we did Dwayne Koroma last year a little bit. He's trying to get the weight on. But it was more their lineup." "And," Hurley added after a slight pause, "Elmer's got a lot of work to do." A couple of other observations from Tuesday night: The Huskies' free-throw shooting over the first two exhibition games hasn't been very impressive. UConn missed five of its first nine from the charity stripe and was just 6-for-12 at halftime. The Huskies improved in the latter half, hitting 10 of 13 to finish a respectable 77 percent for the game. Against Syracuse, UConn also missed half of its 10 first-half free throws and wound up at 67 percent (18-for-27) for the game. Hines, however, was 7-for-8 in that game. Hurley's unbridled love for Michigan State and Hall of Fame coach Tom Izzo continued. "To this day, Coach is a mentor for me and is someone I've tried to model myself after," Hurley said. "He's your coaches' favorite coach." EAST LANSING, MI - OCTOBER 20: Michigan State Spartans head coach Tom Izzo and UConn Huskies head coach Dan Hurley converse before a college basketball exhibition game between the Michigan State Spartans and UConn Huskies on October 20, 2026 at the Breslin Center in East Lansing, MI. (Photo by Adam Ruff/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) (Icon Sportswire/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Indeed, Jim Calhoun was an unabashed fan of Izzo, as well. No doubt, part of Hurley's admiration for Izzo stems from their shared disgust at the current state of college athletics, where 24-year-old Europeans and fifth-year players previously ruled ineligible are popping up on rosters everywhere. On Monday, Kansas got word that former Purdue standout Trey Kaufman-Renn, a 2021 high school graduate who was an NBA Draft pick in June, is now eligible to play. At least for now. Hurley's affection extended to Michigan State's fans, even though a "(Bleep) Dan Hurley!" chant erupted early in the game. Izzo emphatically directed the fans to stop the chant. "We root for Michigan State when they're playing, we've got the ultimate respect," Hurley said. "Obviously, the fans turned on me at different points in the game, and rightfully so. That was the first time seeing the antics. But, as much as they were mean to me, I root for them." He laughed, then added: "Go Sparty." Sign up for the Connecticut Briefing from CT Insider. Get the biggest headlines of the day from our network of journalists around the state. This article originally published at What did Dan Hurley mean by calling UConn's big men ‘Oppenheimer' after preseason win? .

item.title: LeBron James Clashes With Knicks Fans as Spike Lee Plays Peacemaker: ‘I’m From Ohio, Baby’
item.description: Instagram/Sixers New Yorkers weren’t bowing down for King James. LeBron James made his debut with the Philadelphia 76ers in a highly anticipated game against the reigning champions, the New York Knicks , on Tuesday, October 20, there was plenty of trash-talking from the crowd at Madison Square Garden. In one tense moment caught on camera, James, 41, appeared to clap back at fans during the second quarter, per the New York Post . Instagram/House of Highlights “Ain’t nothing soft in the Midwest. I don’t know what the [expletive] you talking about,” the Akron, Ohio, native snapped, according to the outlet, citing video posted on X . “I’m not from the West Coast. I’m from Ohio, baby. I’m not a Midwest kid, I’m an Ohio baby. [Expletive] is you talking about,” the former LA Lakers player continued, before putting his mouthguard back in and returning to the game. The argument seemed to stem from a fan heckling him for living in New York City and commuting to Philadelphia via helicopter, commentator Mike Tirico pointed out, per the Post . Instagram/House of Highlights “Guess who’s playing peacemaker? Spike Lee ,” fellow broadcaster and retired NBA star Reggie Miller said during the broadcast, per the Post . “He’s over here playing peacemaker. Boy, I’ve seen everything.” The Athletic reporter Mike Vorkunov elaborated in an X post that “things got lively enough” that director, in an orange-and-blue striped suit and matching hat, “stood up to try to calm things down and wave the fan off.” AARON JOSEFCZYK/UPI/Newscom/The Mega Agency But at least one New Yorker welcomed James with open arms. Another fan posted a video of Denzel Washington walking across the court to give him a big hug. The 76ers beat the Knicks 106-100. item.title: T.J. Watt’s wife calls out NFL for Paris game
item.description: (Photo by Rich Graessle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers will face the New Orleans Saints in Week 7 in Paris. Many were wondering if the game would get moved due to the ongoing political unrest in the city, but the NFL pushed forward and decided to keep the game in Paris. It’s a questionable decision, to say the least, and it’s not just fans and media who believe it. Dani Watt, the wife of T.J. Watt, is also questioning why the league didn’t move the game. Watt shared an image on her Instagram story that said the NFL would keep the game in Paris, with the caption, “Tell me how this one makes sense???.” T.J. Watt’s wife, Dani, is not happy about the Steelers-Saints game being played in Paris. #Steelers #NFL pic.twitter.com/2Cyt2J1jP6 — Blitzburgh (@Blitz_Burgh) October 20, 2026 The NFL has announced that they will have heightened security for the game, but the point remains that going forward with playing in Paris doesn’t make a ton of sense with everything going on. Let us know what you think in the comments . Be sure to bookmark Behind the Steel Curtain for all the latest news, breakdowns, and more! item.title: ‘This Is a Very Unaware Play’ — Chiefs’ Super Bowl Champion Takes Issue With Xavier Worthy’s ‘Error’ vs. Chargers
item.description: ‘This Is a Very Unaware Play’ — Chiefs’ Super Bowl Champion Takes Issue With Xavier Worthy’s ‘Error’ vs. Chargers The Kansas City Chiefs cruised to another win on Sunday, continuing their undefeated start to the 2026 season. However, that didn’t come without a questionable play from wide receiver Xavier Worthy. The Chiefs led from start to finish against the Los Angeles Chargers, and it never really got testy for Kansas City. But on one of the final plays before halftime, Worthy made a decision that is now getting backlash on social media. Former Chief Mitch Schwartz Calls Out Xavier Worthy’s ‘Error’ Before Halftime The Chiefs were up 16-3 with 14 seconds left in the first half and had the ball at about midfield. Patrick Mahomes hit Worthy on a short crossing route with plenty of green grass in front of him. But it’s the route he took once he caught the ball and how much time he left on the clock that has Super Bowl champion and former Chief Mitch Schwartz calling it an “error.” “I mean look at this it’s just an awful angle there’s a lot more yards there without having to take any extra contact,” Schwartz wrote on X . Prior to that post, Schwartz had pulled the broadcast’s view and thought there were at least 5 more yards available, and added this post once he saw the end zone view. PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Those posts blew up on X, with many people agreeing with Schwartz and others backing Worthy. On the one hand, it’s quite obvious the Chiefs’ receiver could have gotten a handful more yards on the play, and the angle was much straighter out of bounds than it needed to be. On the other hand, Worthy probably didn’t look at the clock mid-play and was told to catch the ball, get the yardage you can, and get out of bounds beforehand. BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN’s Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator So, Schwartz made a third post because his comments went viral. “Did not expect this to blow up the way it has,” Schwartz wrote. “I’ve been extremely complimentary of (Worthy) the last few weeks. He’s playing his best ball by far. This was the one blemish I saw, and I think it’s an error on his part. It’s not some massive mistake or huge issue, but yes, I do expect my WR to know that he has ample time to continue getting yards before he needs to dip out of bounds.” “The play started with 14 seconds, and he caught a short pass in stride,” Schwartz added. “There’s zero reason to immediately run out of bounds. As we can see, there’s a lot of space there to get at least 5 more yards without having to take any contact. “I’m sorry this has turned into a very negative thing. We shouldn’t all be crapping on him because he is playing much better. But to me, this is a very unaware play, and I think it’s fair to be critical, even if it’s not a huge one in the grand scheme of things.” The Chiefs would go on to make the field goal before halftime and lead 19-3 at the break. The final score was 22-6. The Chiefs are 5-0 on the season,

item.title: John Daly has a new Masters week deal in Augusta after longtime Hooters tradition
item.description: John Daly’s Masters-week tradition in Augusta isn’t going anywhere. In fact, it’s getting bigger. Topgolf announced a multi-year partnership with the two-time major champion that will bring Daly back to its Augusta, Georgia, location during Masters week in 2027 and 2028, extending a relationship that began with his appearances there in 2026. It’s the latest chapter in Daly’s long-running connection to Augusta, one that took an unexpected turn when the city’s Hooters closed. For years, Daly was practically as much a part of Masters week as the traffic on Washington Road. He regularly set up shop at the Augusta Hooters , selling merchandise, signing autographs and taking photos with fans. According to ESPN, Daly made nearly $800,000 during Masters week in 2024. DCP finals: Finalists for 2027 Drive, Chip and Putt National Finals announced That tradition appeared to be in jeopardy when Hooters closed more than 30 company-owned restaurants, including its Augusta location. The company filed for bankruptcy in March 2025 after accumulating $376 million in debt and later moved toward a franchise-only business model. But Daly quickly found another landing spot. Augusta television station WRDW reported that Top Dawg Tavern, located almost directly across the street from the former Hooters where Daly once parked his RV, would host him during Masters week. Now Topgolf is getting into the John Daly business, too. The new partnership follows Daly’s appearances at Topgolf Augusta during the 2026 Masters and will expand beyond Georgia with appearances at Topgolf venues around the country, branded content and other experiences. “I love the vibe at Topgolf,” Daly said. “It’s a place where you can smash a golf ball, listen to music, have a drink and enjoy yourself with friends and family. That’s my kind of golf.” The partnership also includes the return of Topgolf Nights beginning Oct. 22, along with John Daly-branded merchandise and two ready-to-drink cocktails that will be offered at 55 Topgolf locations. “John Daly is a one-of-a-kind icon who completely disrupted this sport by refusing to be anyone but himself,” Topgolf CEO David McKillips said. “At Topgolf, we pride ourselves on breaking down barriers so anyone can play, which is exactly what makes this partnership so natural and exciting.” For Augusta, though, there’s more coming. Topgolf said Daly will make appearances at its Augusta location during Masters week in both 2027 and 2028, with details about a new event involving Daly expected to be announced before next year’s tournament. Daly made 12 appearances in the Masters, with his best finish coming in 1993 when he tied for third. Tim Schmitt is the managing editor of Golfweek and the golf coordinator for the USA Today Network. This article originally appeared on Golfweek: John Daly has a new Masters week deal in Augusta after longtime Hooters tradition
