Augusta television station WRDW reported that Top Dawg Tavern, located almost directly across the street from the former Hooters where Daly once parked his RV, would host him during Masters week. Now Topgolf is getting into the John Daly business, too. The new partnership follows Daly’s appearances at Topgolf Augusta during the 2026 Masters and will expand beyond Georgia with appearances at Topgolf venues around the country, branded content and other experiences. “I love the vibe at Topgolf,” Daly said. “It’s a place where you can smash a golf ball, listen to music, have a drink and enjoy yourself with friends and family. That’s my kind of golf.” The partnership also includes the return of Topgolf Nights beginning Oct. 22, along with John Daly-branded merchandise and two ready-to-drink cocktails that will be offered at 55 Topgolf locations. “John Daly is a one-of-a-kind icon who completely disrupted this sport by refusing to be anyone but himself,” Topgolf CEO David McKillips said. “At Topgolf, we pride ourselves on breaking down barriers so anyone can play, which is exactly what makes this partnership so natural and exciting.” For Augusta, though, there’s more coming. Topgolf said Daly will make appearances at its Augusta location during Masters week in both 2027 and 2028, with details about a new event involving Daly expected to be announced before next year’s tournament. Daly made 12 appearances in the Masters, with his best finish coming in 1993 when he tied for third. Tim Schmitt is the managing editor of Golfweek and the golf coordinator for the USA Today Network. item.title: Shaun Maloney: We need to take recent positives into Celta Vigo game
item.description: Shaun Maloney: We need to take recent positives into Celta Vigo game Celtic are aiming to take an impressive weekend performance against Hearts into matchday three of their UEFA Europa League campaign when they play host to Celt Vigo. And on the back of the 7-1 thrashing of Hearts , the Hoops go into Thursday night’s match full of confidence. Neither side has managed to chalk up any points from their opening two league phase fixtures, so that will obviously have changed come the final whistle tomorrow night. And the Scottish Champions are hoping that it will be three points on the board after the clash with their Spanish opponents. Assistant manager, Shaun Maloney was on press duties at Celtic Park this afternoon (Wednesday), and he reflected on the boost that the emphatic league win on Sunday will give to the Celtic squad. “When you have that sort of result, it obviously brings confidence to the players – some individual and obviously the team,” he said. “I'd say the week that we've had coming back has been pretty positive. It was a really difficult game in Benfica, but the second half sort of led into the Hearts game because it was a really difficult period in that first 30 minutes. 'But what the guys showed in trying to go toe-to-toe with Benfica in that second half sort of led us to the game against Hearts and probably even further back with the Motherwell performance as well.' Commenting on the Celta Vigo game, the Celtic assistant manager said: “It’s going to be a very different game. I think it sounds really simple, but some of the basics that we did – we had to outrun Hearts in certain areas and we did. The 50-50s came out on our side in that game. “There are some fundamental things about a game of football that we got right in that game, we got right in the second half of Benfica, and those sorts of things are probably the challenges we've had since the start of the season. “With the ball, we can be really creative. We just need to have the same level without the ball consistently and against Hearts we did. We'll definitely need that tomorrow night. “Our home form is probably going to dictate whether we go through or not,” he said. “I know we can win away from home, but the home games are really big, and I think probably what we want to see is as staff is a continuation of what we saw at Motherwell, periods against Benfica and then obviously Hearts. 'I think if we can get a really committed team with and without the ball, then we can definitely win this game.' “Celta are a good side and they can definitely hurt you. So we need both sides, and I just want to see us continue on from the last seven to 10 days on that.” In terms of a squad update, Shaun Maloney confirmed that Cameron Carter-Vickers and Alistair Johnston are both back training, and while neither player will play in Thursday night’s Europa League tie, they could both be available for the weekend trip to Edinburgh to take on Hibernian. item.title: Hot Mic Moment During Oilers-Wild Game Picks Up Offensive Slur on Live Broadcast
item.description: Getty Images Viewers tuning in to the Edmonton Oilers and Minnesota Wild match on Tuesday, October 20, were subjected to some offensive language during a particularly wild hot mic moment. With 11:34 left in the second period, someone on the Wild+ broadcast made a derogatory remark about goalies. “Every goalie’s [slur],” a man’s voice said in footage shared widely on social media. “Insane hot mic,” one viewer captioned the clip on X , which has now been viewed almost 2 million times. It’s unclear who made the remark, which only appears to have aired on the Wild’s broadcast of the game. The Oilers broadcast, meanwhile, is available on Hulu and includes live analysis from play-by-play announcer Anthony LaPanta and color commentator Ryan Carter — neither of whom appeared to have made the slur or even heard it. This is the version which aired on Canada’s Sportsnet, per Bring Me The Sports , and the insult wasn’t audible during the live broadcast either. Fans on social media have suggested the comment was actually made by a fan in the stands, as others could be heard laughing about it as well. “People saying its the minnesota broadcast team are insane that is very obviously not their voices and there are people laughing its the crowd,” wrote one viewer on X . X/@yurovss On Threads, another fan wrote , “Idk who said it. It wasn’t the ref making the call and it didn’t sound like LaPanta or Carter either.” Another agreed , adding, “i know our guys voices 😭 like cmon it’s obviously the audience.” Others simply reacted with shock that the offensive word made it onto live television. “Heard this live but then 2nd guessed myself. Didnt think there was any way that was what I heard,” read one comment . On Threads, another added , “Yeah we heard that too…didn’t know people still use that word in that manner. Embarrassing. The giggles also were gross.” Read More From First for Sports LeBron James Clashes With Knicks Fans as Spike Lee Plays Peacemaker: 'I'm From Ohio, Baby' NASCAR Legend Fred Lorenzen Posthumously Diagnosed With CTE, a First for the Sport’s Drivers Knicks Vs. 76ers Season Opener Breaks Decade-Old Record for Most Expensive Regular Season NBA Game Ever This story Hot Mic Moment During Oilers-Wild Game Picks Up Offensive Slur on Live Broadcast first appeared on First for Sports . item.title: Bayern Munich's Joshua Kimmich to miss Arsenal match after bereavement
item.description: Bayern Munich's Joshua Kimmich will miss their upcoming game against Arsenal -Credit:Alexander Hassenstein, Getty Images Joshua Kimmich will be absent from Bayern Munich's match against Arsenal on Wednesday after a death in his family. Kimmich is a pivotal figure for Bayern and would ordinarily be among the first names on the team sheet for Vincent Kompany. However, the German giants confirmed on Wednesday that he would miss the fixture for personal reasons. Bayern said in a statement, via The Mirror : "Due to a death in his immediate family, Joshua Kimmich is not in the squad today for the match against Arsenal London. Erik ten Hag 'embarrassed' by Scott McTominay transfer as ex-Man United manager slams club bosses Cristiano Ronaldo delivers brutal Portugal 'ultimatum' after Jorge Jesus 'broke his word' -Credit:Christina Pahnke - sampics, Corbis via Getty Images "On behalf of the family, we ask that his privacy and grief be respected, and that further inquiries and reporting be refrained from. In deep sympathy, the entire FC Bayern stands by Joshua Kimmich's side." Bayern assistant manager Aaron Danks had raised doubts over Kimmich's availability during Tuesday's pre-match press conference. "For Joshua it is personal reasons. I am not sure what it means for tomorrow," he said. Danks addressed the media in place of manager Kompany, who is battling illness. "Vince has had a virus, and it is important for him to rest," Danks said. "So he is at home. We are taking it day by day. He will play his role in the game whether in the Allianz Arena or not." Bayern will also be missing influential playmaker Michael Olise following his red card in their 3-3 draw against Viking FK last week. Jamal Musiala is similarly sidelined with a thigh injury, making Lennart Karl the likely candidate to slot into the starting lineup. Manuel Neuer, however, is expected to reclaim his spot between the posts after sitting out both the dramatic Viking draw and Saturday's 6-1 demolition of RB Leipzig with a foot complaint. To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE When quizzed on Bayern missing Olise, Mikel Arteta commented: "I don't know [if it is an advantage], I don't want to say who is the best player in these kind of games. "He's out, but when you look at the squad the starting possible XI that they have, you know, first of all, as a team, how incredibly well coached they are, the mindset that they have, the competition that they have in every action and the individual quality moments that they can creator throughout the game when you look at the goals and chances that they generate. "So that's the opposition that you want to be facing and we will be facing tomorrow and we're just going to confront that and go for it." Arsenal head into the game without the injured trio of William Saliba, Christos Tzolis and Piero Hincapié, though Martín Zubimendi could return to the fold after recovering from the injury he picked up against Leeds United.

item.title: Rams’ Davante Adams replacement options following top trade target Terry McLaurin’s injury
item.description: The Los Angeles Rams suddenly have a major hole at wide receiver after Davante Adams suffered a ruptured hamstring that is expected to sideline him for 6-10 weeks. The Rams, of course, will now look to the NFL trade market for another proven receiver. Terry McLaurin seemed like one of the best potential fits, but Washington’s star receiver suffered a season-ending torn patellar tendon just one day after the Adams news. Now, Los Angeles may have to look deeper into the trade market. Keenan Allen and Quentin Johnston remain intriguing possibilities, but Chris Godwin has emerged as another name who could make sense for Sean McVay’s offense. MORE: Bold predictions for Week 7 of 2026 NFL season Keenan Allen remains the safest veteran option Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen speaks with media Wednesday, Aug. 19, 2026, ahead of the Colts’ joint practice with the Atlanta Falcons at Grand Park in Westfield. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Allen would arguably provide the Rams with the closest stylistic replacement for what Adams brings as a veteran presence. The 34-year-old has spent his career becoming one of the NFL’s most reliable route runners and chain movers, and Indianapolis signed him this offseason after his productive 2025 campaign with the Chargers. Allen has 26 receptions for 227 yards and a touchdown through six games in Indianapolis, and his experience could be particularly valuable for Matthew Stafford and McVay. The Colts are also suddenly a team worth monitoring after the organization moved on from general manager Chris Ballard. Rival teams reportedly believe Indianapolis could be open for business ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Quentin Johnston represents a much different type of option. The Chargers receiver is younger and more of a projection, but Los Angeles’ 0-6 start could eventually force the organization to reconsider its roster. Johnston had already been identified as a potential trade candidate before the season deteriorated further. Tampa Bay is now 1-5, and the veteran receiver is playing on a contract that could make him an intriguing asset if the Buccaneers decide their season is headed in the wrong direction. While those numbers are not particularly impressive, the Rams would not necessarily need him to be the dominant receiver he was earlier in his career. With Puka Nacua already serving as the primary weapon, Godwin could instead provide Stafford with another experienced target capable of working underneath and from the slot. The biggest question is whether Tampa Bay would actually move him. The Buccaneers could still view the NFC South as winnable, and Godwin remains an important veteran in their locker room. But if Tampa Bay decides to become a seller, the Rams should at least make the call. Los Angeles has already lost Adams for a significant portion of the season, and McLaurin is no longer an option. McVay has acknowledged the team may need to add another receiver, making the trade market increasingly important. Godwin, Allen and Johnston could give the Rams three very different avenues to address the same problem. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: Eagles rumors: ESPN insider wonders if Jalen Hurts is totally done in Philly
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images. Eagles rumors: ESPN insider wonders if Jalen Hurts is totally done in Philly appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The NFL Players Association (NFLPA) is calling for a thorough investigation into how the NFL handled the situation involving Jalen Hurts , who developed blood clots. They criticized the league for its quick closure of the matter and the lack of a formal review regarding the medical care provided after Hurts played in London, despite an initial calf ultrasound. As discussions about player safety and accountability continue, the long-term implications for the roster are also under intense scrutiny. A report by ESPN, featuring insights from Dan Graziano and Jeremy Fowler, raised questions about whether Jalen Hurts has a future with the Philadelphia Eagles . Graziano pointed out that while Hurts is signed through 2028, the guaranteed money in his contract decreases to $22 million of his $51.5 million salary in 2027. This situation could create challenges during the offseason, especially as young stars like Quinyon Mitchell and Cooper DeJean become eligible for contract extensions. Fowler emphasized the uncertainty surrounding Hurts’s future, noting that the Eagles did not extend his contract last offseason, despite his impressive 59-28 starting record. This leaves Hurts’s status with the team completely up in the air. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The chaotic situation has drawn sharp criticism from analysts. Sports media personality Nick Kostos recently expressed his discontent with the Eagles’ handling of Hurts’ health on the “Football America” podcast, calling it the most outrageous story he has encountered in his career. He remarked that the franchise is fortunate that the star quarterback did not suffer a fatal incident on the field. Related: With Jalen Hurts out indefinitely, the Eagles have a golden opportunity to Trust the Process Related: NFL media member goes off on Eagles’ ‘bats***’ handling of Jalen Hurts’ blood clot

item.title: Raiders Issued Strong Fernando Mendoza Take Amid Three-Game Losing Skid
item.description: (Photo By Winslow Townson/Getty Images) Getty After a 3-0 start, the Las Vegas Raiders have dropped three straight games, with the latest loss coming to the Buffalo Bills in Week 6. Moreover, in Week 5, head coach Klint Kubiak decided to give Fernando Mendoza his regular-season debut in the loss to the New England Patriots. Amid the Raiders’ losing streak, the conversation is now about whether the team should start the Mendoza era. Nonetheless, former NFL QB Kurt Warner believes that now is not the right time for Las Vegas to turn to the No. 1 pick in the 2027 NFL Draft and have him start over Kirk Cousins. “In my opinion, I don’t think they should as of yet,” Warner said during an Oct. 20 appearance on “The Rich Eisen Show.” “Again, I believe this team is not a great football team, but they’ve got some key pieces, including Kirk Cousins, that are making them competitive every time out. “I just think it’s too early right now, with how competitive and how well Kirk is playing, to go to Fernando just yet. item.title: Brewers World Series costs: How high have prices soared since 1982?
item.description: Things have changed since the last time the Milwaukee Brewers played in a World Series. In 1982, when the Brewers ultimately lost to the St. Louis Cardinals in their first World Series, the cost of a hot dog at County Stadium was $1.10. A 16-ounce beer cost $1.60 – and if you could track down an aisle vendor, a 12-ounce beer would go for $1.40. Now, a junior hot dog at American Family Field will cost you $4 and a domestic beer could set you back about $13 at most of the draft bars in the stadium. A stadium representative told the Journal Sentinel beer prices vary depending on brand and size, but a standard Miller Lite comes out to $13.24. But if you're thinking those older prices are outrageously low, take a look at a column by Mike Kupper published in The Milwaukee Journal on July 8, 1982. "No, I don't think you could really call it a bargain," Kupper wrote. "It's no more expensive than many other family entertainments, but it's not cheap, either, unless you're willing to put up with the no-frills, bare-bones approach. And I ask you: What would baseball be without a beer or a hot dog?" Here's the concessions prices Kupper reported in 1982 and how they compare to current prices. Concession 1982 Price 2026 Price Hot dog $1.10 $4.00 Bratwurst $1.30 $8.00 Soda (medium) $0.90 $4.00 Beer $1.60 (16 oz. draft) $13.24 Popcorn $1.75 $4.00 Nachos $1.40 $4.00 Peanuts $0.80 $4.00 Lots of historic baseball staple snacks end up on the stadium's 414 Menu, an updated concession menu that cut many snacks down to $4 in 2023. The rising concession prices have outpaced inflation over the years. If you only adjusted for inflation, a $1.10 hot dog in July 1982 would cost $3.80 in 2026, while that $1.60 beer would be about $5.53, according to the Consumer Price Index calculator . But concessions might feel like a steal compared to tickets. Most tickets to the 1982 World Series cost between $8 and $18, according to multiple news outlets and Brewers fans on social media . Tickets to Game 1 of the 2026 World Series in Milwaukee are selling for $2,700 or more. But other than tickets, one of the most sizeable increases shows up in the cost of parking. "It costs $3 these days to park in the stadium lot, which is excessive, considering that normally there still is a healthy walk involved after parking," Kupper reported in 1982. On a regular game day in 2026, parking at American Family Field costs $44. And, according to StubHub, parking passes for the 2026 World Series start at $119. On Oct. 20, 2026, the average gallon of gas in Wisconsin cost $4.18. Minimum wage in Wisconsin was $3.25 an hour, and $1.95 an hour for tipped employees, in 1982. item.title: Butch Harmon urges the PGA Tour to make big change in the absence of Tiger Woods and Phil Mickelson
item.description: Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images Butch Harmon has been around the very highest level of the game for more than six decades now. Harmon has coached some of the greatest golfers ever to have graced the game, including Tiger Woods, Phil Mickelson and Greg Norman. The 83-year-old is one of the most knowledgeable people in the game, and everything he says always carries real weight. Butch Harmon obviously knows Tiger Woods and Phil Mickelson inside out, but he is also a keen follower of emerging talents coming through the ranks on the PGA Tour . And Harmon has highlighted one thing he believes the PGA Tour needs to do much more of regarding their promotion of the supremely talented batch of youngsters coming through. Butch Harmon urges PGA Tour to make changes in the absence of Tiger Woods and Phil Mickelson While speaking on the No Laying Up Podcast, Harmon was asked to give his opinion on the current state of the game. “ I think we have the best crop of young players we’ve ever had, “ Harmon suggested. They’re unbelievable. That’s the plus side. The downside for TV is that nobody knows who these players are. “ They’ll turn on the TV, and if some of the stars aren’t up there, and they see these guys 20, 23, under, they go, I don’t know who that is, and they change the channel. “ So I don’t think the PGA Tour does a good enough job of promoting the younger players through special stuff where you can learn about their lives and stuff. “ If you look at young players on the PGA Tour, the DP World Tour, the Asian Tour, they’re unbelievable these kids. There are a lot of them, and there are more of them coming. “ So the game is changing completely to what it used to be because the big stars are not there anymore. Tiger’s gone, Phil’s gone. All the other guys are gone. You know, all the ones you grew up with are all on the Champions Tour now. “ Harmon makes a great point. There are so many incredibly talented young players coming through the ranks on the PGA Tour right now. And the tour really needs to make more of an effort to showcase them. Perhaps a series on The Golf Channel examining the personalities of these players and giving fans a behind the scenes look at their lives would do the trick. This would enable golf fans to forge more of a connection with the young stars of the modern era and perhaps then the likes of Michael Brennan, Jackson Koivun and co. would become the next true superstars of the game.

item.title: Packers Trade Pitch Targets Colts’ 3-Time Pro Bowler for 4th-Round Pick
item.description: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 02: DeForest Buckner #99 of the Indianapolis Colts warms up against the Pittsburgh Steelers in the game at Acrisure Stadium on November 02, 2025 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) Getty The Green Bay Packers have already lost one veteran defensive tackle for the season. Now, a new trade proposal has them looking to the Indianapolis Colts for another established player who could help their defense down the stretch. DeForest Buckner has continued to produce in Indianapolis, but the Colts are 2-4, general manager Chris Ballard has been fired and the 32-year-old made his frustration clear following Sunday’s loss to the Tennessee Titans. With the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline approaching, Green Bay has been named as a potential landing spot for Buckner in a deal that wouldn’t require a premium draft pick. DeForest Buckner Trade Pitch Names Packers as Suitor Bleacher Report’s Kristopher Knox listed Buckner at No. 4 on his Oct. 21 trade block rankings, projecting a 2027 fourth-round pick as the price to acquire him. Knox named the Packers and San Francisco 49ers as potential suitors. The proposal followed the Colts’ decision to fire Ballard on Monday, one day after a 26-20 home loss to the previously winless Titans. Indianapolis named assistant GM Ed Dodds to oversee its personnel department for the remainder of the season. Knox suggested the leadership change could put veteran players on the market if ownership decides to shift its focus toward the future. “Premier defensive tackles generally command strong returns, and Buckner is still one of those, even at 32,” Knox wrote. Buckner has started all six games this season, totaling 26 tackles, four sacks and three passes defended. The three-time Pro Bowler is in the final year of his contract, which could make him a short-term addition for a team pursuing a playoff run. His comments following the loss to Tennessee have also attracted attention. “I’m sick and tired of the same song and dance every year,” Buckner said, via NFL.com’s Kevin Patra . Buckner also said he still had confidence in the people in Indianapolis when asked about the coaching staff and front office. His comments were about the Colts’ struggles, rather than a trade request. DeForest Buckner Could Address Packers’ Injury-Hit Defense Green Bay has a more immediate reason to consider the idea. Defensive tackle Javon Hargrave is out for the season with an Achilles injury. The Packers also placed Jonathan Ford on injured reserve before their Week 6 victory over the Dallas Cowboys . The team signed former first-round pick Mazi Smith to its practice squad Tuesday, but that move provides depth rather than the proven interior pass rush Buckner could offer alongside Devonte Wyatt. The Packers are 4-2 following their 23-13 win over Dallas, their third straight victory. Their defense intercepted Dak Prescott twice and held the Cowboys to 48 rushing yards. Even with that performance,

Defensive tackle Javon Hargrave is out for the season with an Achilles injury. The Packers also placed Jonathan Ford on injured reserve before their Week 6 victory over the Dallas Cowboys . The team signed former first-round pick Mazi Smith to its practice squad Tuesday, but that move provides depth rather than the proven interior pass rush Buckner could offer alongside Devonte Wyatt. The Packers are 4-2 following their 23-13 win over Dallas, their third straight victory. Their defense intercepted Dak Prescott twice and held the Cowboys to 48 rushing yards. Even with that performance, injuries along the front remain an issue as Green Bay pushes toward the second half of the season. He has since become one of its most established defensive leaders, but he hasn’t played in a postseason game since that first season with the Colts. For the Packers, Knox’s suggested fourth-round price would offer a chance to add an experienced pass rusher without parting with an early selection. Indianapolis would have to decide whether getting that pick is worth losing one of its most productive defenders midway through another difficult season. item.title: Albany native, Green Tech grad U-Mier Graham ready to contribute immediately for UAlbany men's basketball
item.description: U-Mier Graham, who once starred at Green Tech, is expected to contribute as a freshman this season for the UAlbany men's basketball team. (Lori Van Buren/Times Union) ALBANY - Nagging injuries have made it tough for the University at Albany men's basketball team to consistently do 5-on-5 work this preseason. On one of those rare occasions last week when the Great Danes did get to do just that, though, one of the members playing among the presumed starting five was a bit surprising. Freshman forward U-Mier Graham, an Albany native and former Green Tech High standout, was part of UAlbany's first unit playing power forward. He was joined in the frontcourt by Erwann Bussing and Papa Kounta, with Ollie Engen and fellow Albany native Zacharie Matulu at the guard spots. There's no guarantee that the 6-foot-7 Graham will be in the starting lineup when UAlbany opens its season Nov. 2 against Rhode Island College, especially as fellow forwards Abdoulaye Fall and Pedro Santos make their way back from injury, but the freshman has been one of the players who has impressed UAlbany coach Dwayne Killings the most since arriving on campus. "He's played really well at the four and the five," Killings said. In high school, Graham was a Times Union all-star as both a junior and a senior, averaging double-digit points and rebounds in both campaigns. As a junior in 2024, he helped lead Green Tech to a Class AAA state championship, while his senior season ended with a Section 2 final loss to eventual state champion Shaker. Graham then spent a post-graduate year at The Knox School on Long Island playing under Jared Grasso, the former head coach at UAlbany's America East rival Bryant. That post-grad season helped Graham expand his on-court game, but it was his growth from being away from home that aided the forward most in his transition to college basketball. "It gave me a chance to learn how to be away from my family for a long time," he said. "I just knew that I could always look for my teammates - my brothers - and make sure that we're connected." Like Matulu, a Shaker High grad and UAlbany's top returning scorer, Graham said he's thrilled to be playing at home in front of local crowds, with friends and family easily able to attend the Great Danes' home games at Broadview Center. But, Graham said, he's also adamant in keeping his home life and his basketball life as separate entities to avoid distractions. "I'm glad to be back home, but it's good that I separate home from basketball, because I'm here to do a job," he said. "I'm here to work. That's the goal." item.title: Bayern Munich v Arsenal Preview: Team News, Predicted Lineup & Score Prediction
item.description: Bayern Munich v Arsenal Preview: Team News, Predicted Lineup & Score Prediction It’s matchday, Gooners! And what a Champions League night we have ahead of us! Arsenal are heading to the Allianz Arena to face Bayern Munich, with two European victories already under our belts and a formidable challenge awaiting in Germany. After a hard-fought 1-0 victory at Napoli and a convincing 3-0 win over Lille , Mikel Arteta’s side are chasing a remarkable 15th consecutive Champions League league-phase victory. But Bayern Munich at home? That’s another challenge entirely. Bayern’s fortress meets Arsenal’s European momentum Bayern have lost just once in their last 31 Champions League home matches, winning 24. That’s quite a record, although Arsenal have reason to approach tonight with confidence. Our 3-1 victory over Bayern at the Emirates last November remains the only occasion in their last 23 European matches that they’ve lost by more than one goal. And Arsenal’s away form in Europe is impressive too, unbeaten in eight Champions League away matches, with six victories and five clean sheets. Bayern are unbeaten in the Bundesliga this season and arrive fresh from a 6-1 victory over Leipzig. However, their recent 3-3 Champions League draw against Viking exposed defensive vulnerabilities. As Arsenal’s official match preview highlights, Bayern have managed just three clean sheets in their opening ten matches across competitions. There will be opportunities tonight. The question is whether we can take them! (Photo by Richard Heathcote/Getty Images) Team news and the battle that could decide tonight There’s welcome news for Arsenal, with Martin Zubimendi available again after recovering from injury. Piero Hincapié remains unavailable, alongside William Saliba and Christos Tzolis. Bayern also have problems. Michael Olise is suspended , Jamal Musiala is injured, and Manuel Neuer remains a doubt. But Harry Kane will demand plenty of attention. His movement into midfield could cause problems for Arsenal’s defensive organisation, while Luis Díaz offers serious pace and attacking threat out wide. Arteta is clearly relishing the occasion. “I’m really looking forward to the game, this is the stage, this is the kind of team, this is the kind of coach, this is the kind of club, the stadium that you want to be involved in.” Predicted Lineup: Raya; Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Guimarães, Rice; Saka, Ødegaard, Madueke; Gyökeres Score prediction: Bayern Munich 1-2 Arsenal COYG! So, Gooners, do you share Arteta’s enthusiasm? Can Arsenal silence the Allianz Arena and make it three Champions League victories from three? What’s your score prediction and predicted lineup tonight? item.title: Columns and Courts: Mizzou Tennis takeaways
item.description: Missouri women’s tennis has spent the opening months of its fall season adjusting to a new coaching staff, evaluating its roster and building chemistry as the Tigers prepare for the spring dual-match schedule. Head coach Robin Goodman, who was hired in May 2026, has used the fall tournaments to establish his expectations and learn more about a roster that features just one returning player from last season. Associate head coach Manny Raga and assistant coach Bronte Murgett have joined Goodman in helping guide the program through the transition. The fall schedule has provided an early opportunity for the staff to evaluate individual performances while emphasizing the importance of competing together, particularly as the team works toward its goals for the upcoming spring season. Building chemistry under a new staff The ITA Central Regional Championships marked an important checkpoint for Missouri, bringing together all three coaches and the Tigers’ nine player roster for the tournament. Missouri recorded 11 wins on the opening day of competition Thursday, Oct. 15, giving the team early momentum and opportunities to test itself against regional competition. Goodman was encouraged by the team’s willingness to compete and support one another throughout the tournament, pointing to those qualities as important parts of the program’s development. “Another great tournament for us,” Goodman said. “Really proud of the way these girls fight and their willingness to support one another.” The tournament also gave the coaching staff more time to assess how its players respond to competitive situations and work alongside their teammates. With a brand new group coming together, those experiences could prove valuable when Missouri transitions to the spring season, when dual matches will place a greater emphasis on collective results. A young roster gains valuable experience Missouri entered the fall with nine players, seven of whom are freshmen, alongside sophomore Alex Ackman and junior Millie Skelton, a transfer from SMU. Ackman is well documented as the only player returning from last season’s roster, making the early tournaments especially important for a team learning to compete under a new staff. The Tigers opened the fall at the Husker Invitational in September before traveling to Charlotte for the 49er Invite. Missouri earned 12 wins against opponents including Charlotte, Clemson, Maryland and Rutgers at the latter tournament, continuing a productive start to the season. The ITA Central Regional Championships provided another encouraging result, as Missouri finished with 17 wins across three days of competition. item.content:encoded: Missouri women’s tennis has spent the opening months of its fall season adjusting to a new coaching staff, evaluating its roster and building chemistry as the Tigers prepare for the spring dual-match schedule. Head coach Robin Goodman, who was hired in May 2026, has used the fall tournaments to establish his expectations and learn more about a roster that features just one returning player from last season. Associate head coach Manny Raga and assistant coach Bronte Murgett have joined Goodman in helping guide the program through the transition. The fall schedule has provided an early opportunity for the staff to evaluate individual performances while emphasizing the importance of competing together, particularly as the team works toward its goals for the upcoming spring season. Building chemistry under a new staff The ITA Central Regional Championships marked an important checkpoint for Missouri, bringing together all three coaches and the Tigers’ nine player roster for the tournament. Missouri recorded 11 wins on the opening day of competition Thursday, Oct. 15, giving the team early momentum and opportunities to test itself against regional competition. Goodman was encouraged by the team’s willingness to compete and support one another throughout the tournament, pointing to those qualities as important parts of the program’s development. “Another great tournament for us,” Goodman said. “Really proud of the way these girls fight and their willingness to support one another.” The tournament also gave the coaching staff more time to assess how its players respond to competitive situations and work alongside their teammates. With a brand new group coming together, those experiences could prove valuable when Missouri transitions to the spring season, when dual matches will place a greater emphasis on collective results. A young roster gains valuable experience Missouri entered the fall with nine players, seven of whom are freshmen, alongside sophomore Alex Ackman and junior Millie Skelton, a transfer from SMU. Ackman is well documented as the only player returning from last season’s roster, making the early tournaments especially important for a team learning to compete under a new staff. The Tigers opened the fall at the Husker Invitational in September before traveling to Charlotte for the 49er Invite. Missouri earned 12 wins against opponents including Charlotte, Clemson, Maryland and Rutgers at the latter tournament, continuing a productive start to the season. The ITA Central Regional Championships provided another encouraging result, as Missouri finished with 17 wins across three days of competition. Ackman and freshman Daria Budko advanced in the singles main draw, while all four Missouri doubles teams won their opening matches to give the Tigers a 4-0 start in doubles play. The tournament also showed the challenges that come with competing against established programs. Ackman and freshman Danielle Chapman both played three-set matches in the main draw’s round of 32 but were unable to advance, providing experience in high-pressure situations that could benefit them later in the season. Looking ahead to the spring Missouri’s early results suggest the team is making progress, but the primary takeaway is the development happening beyond the win-loss column. Goodman and his staff are establishing expectations for consistency, discipline and communication while the players learn how to compete alongside one another. The Tigers will continue that process at the Jae Foundation Invite, hosted by TCU in Fort Worth, Texas, from Oct. 22-24. The tournament offers another opportunity for Missouri’s young roster to gain experience. With a new coaching staff and an almost entirely new roster, Missouri still has plenty to establish before the spring season begins. However, the Tigers’ steady collection of wins and growing team chemistry have given Goodman an encouraging starting point as he works to build the program’s future. Tiger Top Spin will be back next Monday recapping the Jae Foundation Invite. Columns and Courts will return next Wednesday looking forward to ITA sectionals.

item.title: Bears vs. Patriots: Can Grady Jarrett beat the ailing Pats interior?
item.description: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles scrambles from Grady Jarrett #50 of the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s a quick turnaround week, which always magnifies the injury report for teams. The Bears are not without injuries, as Kyle Monangai, Jonah Jackson, and TJ Edwards have all been sidelined this week. The Patriots, however, had their OL decimated on Sunday against the Jets. Guards Alijah Vera-Tucker and Ben Brown, and Tackle Morgan Moses all had varying injuries Sunday that put their statuses in question for Thursday’s matchup in Chicago. This adds to an already ailing OL in New England with Greg Van Roten, Michael Owenwu, and Marcus Bryant on IR. This leaves the Bears with a golden opportunity — get pressure up the middle, and disrupt Drake Maye quickly. The third year QB currently has his highest career pressure % at 26.2%, an uptick of 5% from last season. Losing three starters isn’t going to help. You have to expect a combination of rookie Caleb Lomu, Matt Pryor, and Walter Rouse to fill in for their teammates’ absences. Lomu and Rouse have about 300 snaps in their careers between them, while Pryor — a vet that Bears fans are very familiar with — has a fair amount of experience and is capable of providing quality starts. Still, this opens up a major opportunity for the Bears. Enter Grady Jarrett. Jarrett, one of the big DL acquisitions in the 2025 offseason, has been more disruptive in 2026 than 2025, despite his numbers still lagging. While he hasn’t yet recorded a sack, he has 5 pressures, 3 hurries, and two QB hits through 6 games this season. Much of his game needs to be seen live, though, as his presence has been felt more often, setting up others for sacks or impact plays. For instance, watch this sack Dayo Odeyingbo has on Jalen Hurts. Grady Jarrett’s stunt and pressure forces Hurts to step up, right into the arms of Dayo: Dayo Odeyingbo comes up BIG for the SACK on Jalen Hurts 😤 pic.twitter.com/XL4pIuvirJ — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) September 29, 2026 This is the type of impact Jarrett is going to have to make on Thursday against a jump start Patriots squad. After starting the season 1-2, New England is on a bit of a tear, winning their last three games by a combined 38 points. Maye is at the center of that, and he has proven to have a propensity for going downfield, as evidenced by his 5th-best 8.0 yards per pass attempt. The Packers game illustrated the Bears’ weakness in covering deep passes, and their need to maintain several defenders in coverage against QBs with a strong deep ball. So getting pressure on four man fronts will be even more critical for the Bears. With Grady Jarrett going up against two potential backups in Matt Pryor and Walter Rouse, he could do some serious damage in limiting Maye’s ability to throw downfield. If the Bears are to win this Thursday, I think that Jarrett

item.title: Scottish FA confirm match officials for Celtic’s trip to Easter Road
item.description: Scottish FA confirm match officials for Celtic’s trip to Easter Road The Scottish FA have confirmed the match officials for Celtic’s Scottish Premiership encounter against Hibernian at Easter Road on Sunday. Referee Ryan Lee checks the VAR screen during the Scottish Premiership match between St. Mirren and Celtic at St Mirren Park on September 05, 2026. (Photo by Zak Mauger/Getty Images) Martin O’Neill’s side travel to Edinburgh looking to build on their emphatic 7-1 victory over Hearts last weekend, which provided a significant boost to confidence following a difficult period for the Scottish champions. The Hoops currently sit at the top of the Premiership table, while Hibernian find themselves rooted to the bottom following a disappointing start to the campaign. New Hibs manager Marink Reedijk has endured a difficult introduction to life at Easter Road, losing both of his opening matches in charge, including last weekend’s defeat to Falkirk. Ahead of Sunday’s meeting, the Scottish FA have now confirmed the refereeing team responsible for overseeing the encounter. Ryan Lee has been appointed as the match referee, with Chris Rae and Scott Anderson serving as his assistants. Iain Snedden will take up fourth official duties, while experienced referee Nick Walsh will oversee VAR operations, assisted by Duncan Williams. item.title: Confirmed Man United XI vs Como
item.description: Confirmed Man United XI vs Como Manchester United visit Como today for an early kick-off in the Champions League. Head coach Michael Carrick remains under intense pressure having failed to beat Leeds United on Sunday and has to deal with the absence of a host of first-team stars. Here is the confirmed line-up for the game. Goalkeeper and Defence Senne Lammens is in goal. Diogo Dalot is at right back. Harry Maguire continues at centre-back. More to follow … Leny Yoro is suspended. Luke Shaw, Lisandro Martinez and Patrick Dorgu are all injured and Ayden Heaven is unwell. Midfield Carlos Baleba retains his place in central midfield and is partnered again by Andrey Santos, with Youri Tielemans playing ahead of them. Kobbie Mainoo did not travel, and Manu Ugarte has a long-term injury. Attack Bruno Fernandes stays in a forward role, with Bryan Mbeumo retaining his place up front. Amad continues on the right side of midfield. Ben Sesko is out injured. Marcus Rashford is carrying a knock. Substitutes To follow. Final Thoughts Featured image by Jan Kruger via Getty Images online polls

item.title: How Arsenal could beat Juventus to prolific German star
item.description: How Arsenal could beat Juventus to prolific German star Nicolo Tresoldi has emerged as one of the most exciting young forwards in Europe, and his Champions League hat-trick against Inter Milan has increased Juventus’ interest in signing him . The Club Brugge striker is attracting attention after his impressive performances, with several clubs now considering a move for his signature. Juventus could regret not pursuing him more seriously during the summer transfer window. The Bianconeri concentrated much of their effort on bringing Randal Kolo Muani from Paris Saint-Germain and may have missed an opportunity to sign Tresoldi, who had already shown his quality last season. His continued development at Club Brugge has made him an increasingly attractive target. It is perhaps surprising that no major club secured his services during the previous transfer window, but his recent performances have ensured that interest is growing. Arsenal push to sign Tresoldi in January According to The Sun , Arsenal are keen to move for Tresoldi in January rather than wait until the end of the season. The Gunners are reportedly determined to strengthen their attacking options, and the striker has emerged as a potential target. Arsenal could also make changes to their forward line, with Viktor Gyokeres potentially leaving in a future transfer window. If that happens, signing Tresoldi could become an important part of their recruitment plans. However, securing the Club Brugge forward would require a significant financial commitment. Juventus are also interested, but they may be reluctant to spend the amount required to complete a January deal. That could give Arsenal an advantage in the race, particularly if they are prepared to meet Club Brugge’s demands during the winter window. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images) Juventus could wait until the summer Juventus have not necessarily lost their opportunity to sign Tresoldi. If the striker remains at Club Brugge until the end of the season, the Bianconeri could revisit their interest after making sales and creating more room in their transfer budget. Waiting, however, would carry risks. Arsenal could secure an agreement in January, leaving Juventus to consider alternative targets if the forward moves to the Premier League. Tresoldi would also need to decide which destination best suits his ambitions. A move to England could appeal to him, but Juventus could still offer an attractive opportunity if they can put together a convincing proposal. For now, Arsenal’s reported willingness to act in January could prove decisive. Juventus may need to reconsider their financial approach if they want to compete for the striker’s signature.

item.title: Giants Trade Pitch Sends RB Cam Skattebo to Super Bowl Contender
item.description: New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo. Getty It’s pretty obvious that New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh has reached the end of his rope with running back Cam Skattebo — a slow progression that started with an offseason of missteps and culminated in Harbaugh benching Skattebo in Week 6 after fumbles became an issue that cost his team wins. Skattebo will only have trade value for the Giants right now, and they need to move him by the November 10 trade deadline if they want any return on their investment. One team that might leap at giving up a Day 3 pick for Skattebo is the Super Bowl-contending Buffalo Bills, where Skattebo could be a great change-of-pace back alongside starter and NFL All-Pro James Cook — another player with fumbling issues. In this case, the Giants might expect a 6th- or 7th-round pick back — if not, they might cut Skattebo outright after the trade deadline. “The Giants would also love to alter things at running back, apparently,” ESPN’s Dan Graziano wrote on October 21 . “The new coaching staff has clearly soured on Cam Skattebo, the Giants just released Najee Harris, and it wouldn’t be shocking to see them add someone from the outside or give Tyrone Tracy Jr. a bigger chance.” Giants Benched Skattebo Against Saints The Giants benched Skattebo, their leading rusher, after a disastrous fumble cost them a Week 5 win against the Washington Commanders — a game that ended in a tie — and he didn’t get any carries in a Week 6 loss to the New Orleans Saints . When asked about benching Skattebo against the Saints — Harbaugh tried to pull off a Jedi mind trick. “We didn’t bench Cam Skattebo,” Harbaugh said. “That wasn’t by design … they were all pretty equal in the first half (with snaps). It wasn’t intentional that he didn’t carry the ball. You’re not thinking about what running back is in the game or how many carries they’re getting … we’re going to give them all equal shots. See who got a hot hand … you’re balancing it between four guys. Do the math.” Harbaugh Called Skattebo ‘Disease’ in Training Camp Harbaugh has been open about his disgust with Skattebo almost since he got the job with the Giants — a stretch that saw Skattebo at the heart of a controversy where he denied concussions and asthma were real things in the offseason as well as a failed backflip attempt during a Fanatics event on a surgically-repaired leg before training camp. During training camp, after one practice in which Skattebo began to draw the ire of his teammates after several bizarre stunts — including running over a linebacker during a non-contact practice — Harbaugh unloaded on him. “He got a 15-yard penalty at the end of practice,” Harbaugh said in August. “Did you see that? Yeah it’s infectious. It can be infectious the other way, an infectious disease type of thing. We want it to be in a positive way.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Giants Trade Pitch Sends RB Cam Skattebo to Super Bowl Contender appeared first on HEAVY

item.title: Toppling Iran government only way to end threat – Netanyahu
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Wednesday that the only way to remove the threat posed by Iran was to topple its government. “Iran wanted to destroy us; we stopped them. They wanted to produce nuclear bombs; we stopped them… Yet they persist,” he said during an election rally in the southern town of Dimona. “Therefore, there is only one way to end this: by toppling this regime.” “This is the directive I have issued to the Israel Defense Forces, to the Mossad, and to all our security branches,” he added, without specifying when or how that directive would be executed. AFP The post Toppling Iran government only way to end threat – Netanyahu appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Como v Manchester United: Champions League – live
item.description: ⚽️ Champions League updates from 5.45pm BST ⚽️ Live scoreboard | Champions League table | Mail Simon Hello world! And welcome to this, a tale of two managers. Poor Michael Carrick, for all his undoubted ability, has been negatively compared for Cesc Fabregas for many years. Back in October 2009 the Guardian’s late, great football correspondent David Lacey wrote a column in praise of the Spaniard’s reliable brilliance – “Bergkamp did have off days, whereas Fabregas just has the odd day off” – in which Carrick was referred to, in passing, as a “gifted water carrier”. And here they are, 17 years and a few days later, up against each other once again, in a different role, one of them obviously good, the other evidently better. Transfermarkt estimates the value of Como’s squad at €568.15m, and Manchester United’s at €928.80m. Como have lost only once in the league this season, while United have won only once. Both have one win and one defeat in their first two Champions League fixtures. And tonight seems destined to be discussed primarily in terms of how it affects Carrick’s standing and chances of long-term employment. Continue reading...

item.title: 3 Toyin Abraham-Inspired Owambe Looks for Your Next Saturday Party
item.description: Three traditional Owambe style moments from Toyin Abraham Ajeyemi featuring velvet, damask, and aso-oke. When Nollywood actor and filmmaker Toyin Abraham Ajeyemi is not busy preparing for her highly anticipated festive cinematic release, Bestie , or writing, producing, and starring in box-office hits like Fate of Alakada , Ijakumo : The Born Again Stripper , and The Ghost and the Tout , she is usually showing us how to nail weekend celebrations. As one of the most prominent faces in Nigerian cinema, her personal style outside the cinema hall has become a major source of fashion inspiration, especially when it comes to pulling off unforgettable Owambe looks. Styling traditional wear for a Saturday party comes down to knowing how to mix colours, textures, and rich fabrics without losing that classic touch. Wearing black and silver to a Nigerian party is all about balance. While dark tones are traditionally avoided for daytime celebrations, pairing a deep black velvet blouse with a metallic silver scalloped-lace skirt completely changes the mood. Draping a silver-grey paisley ipele over the shoulder alongside a matching pleated geleadds instant brightness, while traditional coral beads anchor the entire outfit. Toyin Abraham Ajeyemi showing how to wear black and silver to a Nigerian party. Photo Credit: Toyin Abraham Ajeyemi/Instagram For anyone leaning towards rich jewel tones, crimson velvet offers an instant sense of luxury. Tailoring a solid burgundy velvet gown into a clean, floor-length silhouette provides a sleek base, but adding a patterned teal and magenta damask ipele across one shoulder breaks up the solid fabric. Crowning the look with a structured fan gele in the same damask print brings the entire outfit together. Toyin Abraham Ajeyemi styling crimson velvet and patterned damask for traditional Owambe inspiration. Photo Credit: Toyin Abraham Ajeyemi/Instagram Bright colours always command attention in party halls, and mustard yellow offers a warmer, sophisticated take on sunshine yellow. Tailoring the fabric into a traditional buba and iro set with horizontal black lace bands and tassel-fringe details along the wrapper adds movement and texture. Matching the ensemble with a rounded mustard gele and subtle gold jewellery keeps the palette grounded while letting the traditional silhouette shine. Toyin Abraham Ajeyemi wearing a mustard yellow buba and iro with black lace fringe details for party inspiration. Photo Credit: Toyin Abraham Ajeyemi/Instagram The post 3 Toyin Abraham-Inspired Owambe Looks for Your Next Saturday Party appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.title: Oyo assembly approves Makinde’s N100bn fresh loan, N300bn debt refinancing
item.description: By Adeola Badru The Oyo State House of Assembly has approved a fresh N100 billion loan for Governor Seyi Makinde’s administration to finance infrastructure projects, alongside a separate N300 billion facility to refinance an existing contractors’ loan, in a financial arrangement involving a combined N400 billion. The approval, granted following a request by the governor during plenary on Wednesday, will enable the state government to obtain the new loan from United Bank for Africa (UBA) Plc and transfer its existing N300 billion contractors’ finance facility from Access Bank to the same lender. The decision came as infrastructure financing and the management of public debt remain important issues in the state’s fiscal policy, with the administration seeking additional funds to complete ongoing projects while reducing the interest rate on its existing contractors’ financing obligations. In his letter to the Assembly, addressed to the Speaker, Adebo Ogundoyin, Makinde sought legislative approval for the two financing arrangements, which have separate purposes and financial implications for the state. While the N100 billion facility is intended to provide fresh funding for critical infrastructure projects and accelerate the completion of ongoing developments, the N300 billion component is a refinancing arrangement rather than an additional N300 billion in fresh borrowing. Under the proposed refinancing terms, the existing contractors’ facility obtained from Access Bank at an interest rate of 26 per cent will be transferred to UBA at 22 per cent, representing a reduction of four percentage points. The reduction is expected to lower the interest rate attached to the existing facility, although the actual financial savings will depend on the outstanding balance, repayment schedule and other applicable terms. The separate N100 billion loan, however, will also attract an interest rate of 22 per cent, subject to review in line with prevailing money market conditions. The fresh facility has a repayment tenor of 48 months, with a management fee of 0.25 per cent per annum and an advisory fee of 0.5 per cent annually, both calculated on the outstanding balance. The terms also provided for a three-month moratorium on the repayment of principal and interest. Interest accruing during the moratorium will not be waived but will instead be repaid alongside the fourth, fifth and sixth instalments of the loan. The repayment structure means that the state’s obligations will extend beyond the principal borrowed, with interest charges and applicable fees forming part of the overall cost of the facility. The provision allowing the interest rate to be reviewed in line with market conditions also means that the final cost could depend on how the agreed rate is applied over the repayment period. item.dc:creator: Ayobami
item.content:encoded: By Adeola Badru The Oyo State House of Assembly has approved a fresh N100 billion loan for Governor Seyi Makinde’s administration to finance infrastructure projects, alongside a separate N300 billion facility to refinance an existing contractors’ loan, in a financial arrangement involving a combined N400 billion. The approval, granted following a request by the governor during plenary on Wednesday, will enable the state government to obtain the new loan from United Bank for Africa (UBA) Plc and transfer its existing N300 billion contractors’ finance facility from Access Bank to the same lender. The decision came as infrastructure financing and the management of public debt remain important issues in the state’s fiscal policy, with the administration seeking additional funds to complete ongoing projects while reducing the interest rate on its existing contractors’ financing obligations. In his letter to the Assembly, addressed to the Speaker, Adebo Ogundoyin, Makinde sought legislative approval for the two financing arrangements, which have separate purposes and financial implications for the state. While the N100 billion facility is intended to provide fresh funding for critical infrastructure projects and accelerate the completion of ongoing developments, the N300 billion component is a refinancing arrangement rather than an additional N300 billion in fresh borrowing. Under the proposed refinancing terms, the existing contractors’ facility obtained from Access Bank at an interest rate of 26 per cent will be transferred to UBA at 22 per cent, representing a reduction of four percentage points. The reduction is expected to lower the interest rate attached to the existing facility, although the actual financial savings will depend on the outstanding balance, repayment schedule and other applicable terms. The separate N100 billion loan, however, will also attract an interest rate of 22 per cent, subject to review in line with prevailing money market conditions. The fresh facility has a repayment tenor of 48 months, with a management fee of 0.25 per cent per annum and an advisory fee of 0.5 per cent annually, both calculated on the outstanding balance. The terms also provided for a three-month moratorium on the repayment of principal and interest. Interest accruing during the moratorium will not be waived but will instead be repaid alongside the fourth, fifth and sixth instalments of the loan. The repayment structure means that the state’s obligations will extend beyond the principal borrowed, with interest charges and applicable fees forming part of the overall cost of the facility. The provision allowing the interest rate to be reviewed in line with market conditions also means that the final cost could depend on how the agreed rate is applied over the repayment period. During deliberations, the Deputy Speaker, Muhammad Abiodun Fadeyi, joined other lawmakers, including Adebayo Babajide Gabriel, Olorunpoto Cephas Rahman and Sunkanmi Babalola, in defending continued infrastructure investment as necessary for economic growth and improved public service delivery. The lawmakers cited the LAUTECH Teaching Hospital in Oyo town, the Rashidi Ladoja Circular Road and the Ido-Eruwa Road among the projects whose timely completion, they argued, could deliver wider economic benefits to the state. They maintained that sustained investment in infrastructure would improve connectivity, create employment opportunities, stimulate commercial activities and ease the movement of people and goods across different parts of Oyo State. According to the arguments advanced during the debate, completing ongoing projects would also ensure that funds already committed to construction and other development initiatives translate into tangible benefits for residents rather than leaving projects unfinished despite substantial public expenditure. The lawmakers stressed that infrastructure development should be assessed not only by the amount of money committed but also by the practical benefits delivered to communities, businesses and users of public facilities. The LAUTECH Teaching Hospital project, for instance, was cited in the context of healthcare infrastructure, while the circular road and Ido-Eruwa Road were referenced for their potential contribution to transport connectivity and commercial activity. The approval, therefore, gave the Makinde administration the legislative backing to proceed with the proposed financing arrangements, with the fresh N100 billion intended to support infrastructure delivery and the N300 billion refinancing designed to secure a lower interest rate on an existing obligation. However, the two components carried different implications for the state’s finances. The N100 billion loan will create a new borrowing obligation, while the N300 billion refinancing will restructure an existing facility rather than automatically add the same amount to the state’s fresh debt. Although the reduction from 26 per cent to 22 per cent is expected to ease the cost of the existing contractors’ facility, the new loan’s interest rate, repayment period, management fee, advisory fee and moratorium provisions will determine the total cost of the additional borrowing. Meanwhile, the approval also placed renewed importance on the implementation of the projects for which the new funds are intended, as well as the government’s ability to meet repayment obligations while sustaining spending on other public services. The post Oyo assembly approves Makinde’s N100bn fresh loan, N300bn debt refinancing appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: PHP devs publish critical bug fix as site owners warned: Pull 'em offline if you're unpatched
item.description: PHP developers have released emergency updates for two critical vulnerabilities after cybersecurity authorities warned organizations to patch immediately or consider taking exposed applications offline. PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35 address CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, which can allow unauthenticated remote code execution. The project's developers urged users to update immediately . All PHP installations serving web requests are potentially affected, including deployments using PHP-FPM, Apache's mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP, and LiteSpeed, the developers said. "We consider the risk highest for mod_php, with a demonstrated exploit where an unauthenticated request can trigger the attack before any application code runs." Jake Knott, head of threat intelligence at watchTowr, said: "As expected, watchTowr Intel is already observing in-the-wild exploitation of the latest PHP vulnerabilities, with a variety of vibecoded PoCs already hitting our sensors featuring a variety of 'php2shell' User-Agents. Whilst nobody has been successful to date, we don't expect that will last long." "Where immediate patching is not feasible, organizations should consider isolating internet-facing applications from public networks until a fix is available," CERT-EU said in an advisory issued ahead of the patches. The body lists both vulnerabilities with CVSS scores of 9.2. Finnish government services and websites belonging to the Dutch parliament, cybersecurity authorities, and data protection regulator were taken offline as a precaution. Privacy campaign group noyb also temporarily withdrew its website. PHP "powers WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, and Magento sites, shared hosting platforms, control panels, and an awful lot of software that doesn't even advertise that it runs PHP under the hood," infosec vendor Huntress noted . That makes identifying exposed installations a substantial job. "The number of places you have to go looking to identify vulnerable PHP versions gets very big, very fast," said John Hammond, Huntress's senior principal security researcher. ®

item.title: Disney Officially Announces Glee Reboot Is Happening
item.description: Somehow, Glee has returned. After Ryan Murphy spent most of the press circuit for his recent FX series The Shards talking about how he wanted to reboot his iconic musical comedy-drama series, it has become a reality. On Wednesday, Disney and Hulu announced that the Glee reboot is officially happening, reviving the fan-favorite TV franchise after more than a decade.

item.title: Police arrest 11 suspects for cultism, ATM fraud in Kogi
item.description: Recover 59 ATM cards, two motorcycles, weapons By Boluwaji Obahopo, Lokoja The Kogi State Police Command has arrested 11 suspects over alleged cultism and ATM card-swapping fraud in Itobe, Ofu Local Government Area, and Idah, respectively. The police also recovered 59 ATM cards belonging to different banks, two motorcycles, an axe, a cutlass and a vehicle allegedly used by the suspected fraudsters. The Commissioner of Police, CP Naziru Bello Kankarofi, disclosed this on Wednesday in Lokoja, saying the arrests followed intelligence gathering and surveillance operations targeting suspected criminal activities in the state. He said eight suspected cultists were arrested on October 17, 2026, at a location behind Government Secondary School, Itobe, while three suspected ATM fraudsters were apprehended in Idah on October 20. According to the police, operatives of the Itobe Division, working with local auxiliary forces and community leaders, raided the location at about 5.45 p.m., arresting seven adults and a 14-year-old boy. The suspects were identified as Mutari Ahmed, 26; Mohammed Tairu, 21; Audu Moses Yahaya, 27; Peter Vincent, 28; Progress Aminu, 21; Wisdom Friday, 21; Gabriel Enema, 22; and a minor whose name was withheld. The command said preliminary investigations indicated that the suspects had gathered to appoint a leader for a local cult group. It added that some of them allegedly admitted membership of the Aro-Baga Vikings and Aiye confraternities. The police described the arrests as significant, citing intelligence reports of planned violent clashes between rival cult groups in Itobe and Ejule communities, allegedly fuelled by longstanding rivalries, territorial disputes and reprisal attacks. It said security measures had been strengthened to prevent violence, protect residents and commuters, and address reported threats of reprisals against security personnel and facilities. The case has been transferred to the Violent Crime Response Unit for further investigation, including efforts to apprehend fleeing suspects and identify other persons allegedly connected to the groups. Three arrested over ATM card-swapping fraud In a separate operation, the police arrested three men suspected of involvement in ATM card-swapping fraud in Idah. The suspects were identified as Philip Akiola, 50; Ojo Thomas, 56; and Abdulrauf Suleiman, 48. The command said their arrest followed surveillance launched after a complaint filed on May 19, 2026, by a victim who reportedly lost N1.5 million from his bank account after his ATM card was swapped. The police said operatives recovered 59 ATM cards belonging to different banks and a vehicle allegedly used in the operation. Preliminary investigations indicated that the suspects had allegedly operated the scheme for more than a year, targeting unsuspecting customers at automated teller machines. He said eight suspected cultists were arrested on October 17, 2026, at a location behind Government Secondary School, Itobe, while three suspected ATM fraudsters were apprehended in Idah on October 20. According to the police, operatives of the Itobe Division, working with local auxiliary forces and community leaders, raided the location at about 5.45 p.m., arresting seven adults and a 14-year-old boy. The suspects were identified as Mutari Ahmed, 26; Mohammed Tairu, 21; Audu Moses Yahaya, 27; Peter Vincent, 28; Progress Aminu, 21; Wisdom Friday, 21; Gabriel Enema, 22; and a minor whose name was withheld. The command said preliminary investigations indicated that the suspects had gathered to appoint a leader for a local cult group. It added that some of them allegedly admitted membership of the Aro-Baga Vikings and Aiye confraternities. The police described the arrests as significant, citing intelligence reports of planned violent clashes between rival cult groups in Itobe and Ejule communities, allegedly fuelled by longstanding rivalries, territorial disputes and reprisal attacks. It said security measures had been strengthened to prevent violence, protect residents and commuters, and address reported threats of reprisals against security personnel and facilities. The case has been transferred to the Violent Crime Response Unit for further investigation, including efforts to apprehend fleeing suspects and identify other persons allegedly connected to the groups. Three arrested over ATM card-swapping fraud In a separate operation, the police arrested three men suspected of involvement in ATM card-swapping fraud in Idah. The suspects were identified as Philip Akiola, 50; Ojo Thomas, 56; and Abdulrauf Suleiman, 48. The command said their arrest followed surveillance launched after a complaint filed on May 19, 2026, by a victim who reportedly lost N1.5 million from his bank account after his ATM card was swapped. The police said operatives recovered 59 ATM cards belonging to different banks and a vehicle allegedly used in the operation. Preliminary investigations indicated that the suspects had allegedly operated the scheme for more than a year, targeting unsuspecting customers at automated teller machines. According to the command, the alleged method involved one suspect observing a victim’s personal identification number (PIN) while another created a distraction, allowing them to swap the victim’s card. The suspects would then allegedly use the captured card and PIN to access the victim’s bank account. The police said the suspects reportedly told investigators that an individual identified as “Sunday”, who was said to be abroad, introduced them to the scheme. Their alleged operations primarily targeted ATM users at branches of First Bank, Union Bank and United Bank for Africa within their area of operation, the command added. The case is being transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department in Lokoja for further investigation. The police advised residents to shield their PINs when using ATMs, decline unsolicited assistance and ensure they retrieve their own cards before leaving the machines. It also urged anyone who suspects an ATM card swap to contact their bank immediately to block the card and report the incident to the police. The command said investigations into both cases were ongoing, adding that all suspects would be treated in accordance with the law and presumed innocent until proven guilty by a court of competent jurisdiction. item.title: Science on the Space Station with NASA Astronaut Jessica Watkins
item.description: NASA/Anil Menon NASA astronaut and Expedition 75 flight engineer Jessica Watkins works inside the Kibo laboratory module’s Life Science Glovebox on Oct. 9, 2026, safely mixing living cell samples with a bioink and then filling a special cartridge with the cell‑ink mixture. The advanced research operations were part of the InSPA‑Auxilium Bioprinter‑Cell Printing investigation, which explores 3D bioprinting cartilage tissue in microgravity of higher quality than that produced on Earth. Results may advance the ability to biomanufacture cartilage, benefiting patients on Earth and crew members on long‑duration space missions. Image credit: NASA/Anil Menon

He told the gathering that campaign logistics would be provided. “All the logistics for our campaign, you will have it. Everything you will have it,” he said. That is inclusivity. “Today, we have built twelve new police stations with residences in it, where the police people will stay in order to improve our security architecture.. Today, six area councils we have can boast of roads going to their various areas. It was not like that before,” he said. item.title: ‘I’m always being real’: what on earth persuades disgraced people like Elizabeth Holmes to let the cameras in?
item.description: With You Can See Everything, Holmes joins other such high-profile subjects as Lance Armstrong, Imelda Marcos and Anthony Weiner to allow film-makers to document their lives. But do they ever come out well? In You Can See Everything, convicted fraudster Elizabeth Holmes invites film-makers Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim into her home in a supposed act of “radical transparency”. Holmes is filmed, along with her partner, Billy Evans, and their two young children, in the weeks before starting a prison sentence for defrauding Theranos investors. “The best way for people to see who she is,” Evans says, “is to give as much access as possible into our daily lives”. It may also be the best way to market “Theranos 2.0”, which the couple are working on during filming. But the documentary questions whether Holmes is presenting her authentic self or a manufactured persona. Fielder speaks for the audience when he asks Holmes in a tense exchange whether she’s “being real” with him. “I’m always being real,” she says. That question of authenticity is at the heart of documentary film-making. You Can See Everything is as much about the ambiguous relationship between film-maker and subject as it is about Holmes herself. There is often a power struggle over narrative control in documentaries, with both sides of the dynamic wanting different outcomes from the final film. Watching You Can See Everything inevitably prompts the question: why would Holmes, days before she heads to jail, invite the scrutiny of a film crew? Continue reading...
