item.dc:creator: James Abbott
item.content:encoded: null Key specs Type: Full-frame prime lens Focal length: 16mm Maximum aperture: f/1.8 Lens mount: Sony FE, Nikon Z Weight: 19.4 oz (550 g) Dimensions: 3.35 x 4.06-in (85.2 x 103 mm) Filter thread: 77 mm Release date: May 2023 As you know, prime lenses come in a wide range of sizes and focal lengths, and every once in a while, one comes along and seems to grab you by the scruff of your neck. One such lens is the Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE, which is an impressive and useful lens for astrophotography thanks to its wide-angle field of view and fast maximum aperture. This lens is one of the wider prime lenses that are available and could be one of the best third-party lenses for astrophotography . With a price of just $464 (£533), this is one of the most cost-effective wide-angle primes, but rather than being a second-rate lens, its build quality and image quality are fantastic. It’s not the best, but it’s undoubtedly a lens you would enjoy. Image quality is excellent overall, with no need for lens corrections, except for vignette removal when shooting wide open. With near-perfect sharpness and minimal distortion and aberrations straight out of the camera, perhaps the weight of the lens is a small price to pay. The lens is made up of 15 elements in 12 groups and is built like a tank, with an all-metal body. It is pretty heavy, though, weighing in at 19.4 oz (550 g) despite its relatively compact size. Attach this lens to one of the best Sony cameras and you will have a formidable combination. The 16mm f/1.8 is also available in the Nikon Z-mount. Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE lens review Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE: Performance The Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE has a 77 mm filter thread. (Image credit: James Abbott) Great image quality Impressively sharp at f/1.8 Excellent corner sharpness With a focal length of 16mm and a maximum aperture of f/1.8, this is clearly a great lens for astrophotography from a technical point of view. The light-gathering capabilities are excellent, to say the least, and during testing it was possible to shoot at a range of ISO levels with a moonless sky. Even ISO 800 was often high enough for a correct exposure. The image quality produced by the 16mm f/1.8 is great, with excellent levels of sharpness across the frame. What’s most important here is that even corner sharpness is fantastic when wide open at f/1.8. This is the aperture setting where vignetting is at its strongest, but it reduces drastically when you stop down to f/2.8 and is completely gone by the time you stop down to f/4. Aperture f/2.8, shutter speed 5 secs, ISO 1600. Shot with a Sony A7R V and a Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE on a Three Legged Thing PUNKS Brian 2.0 tripod. James Abbott Aperture f/1.8, shutter speed 5 secs, ISO 400. Shot with a Sony A7R V and a Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE on a Three Legged Thing PUNKS Brian 2.0 tripod. James Abbott Aperture f/2.8, shutter speed 5 secs, ISO 1250. Shot with a Sony A7R V and a Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE on a Three Legged Thing PUNKS Brian 2.0 tripod. James Abbott Aperture f/1.8, shutter speed 5 secs, ISO 800. Shot with a Sony A7R V and a Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE on a Three Legged Thing PUNKS Brian 2.0 tripod. James Abbott Aperture f/1.8, shutter speed 5 secs, ISO 800. Shot with a Sony A7R V and a Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE on a Three Legged Thing PUNKS Brian 2.0 tripod. James Abbott Luckily, though, there is a lens profile in Adobe Camera Raw and Adobe Lightroom that completely removes vignetting. There’s also only minimal chromatic aberration and a tiny amount of barrel distortion, which is impressive given the wide field of view produced by the lens. As mentioned before, sharpness is great wide open and improves incrementally as you stop down up to the sweet spot of the lens, which is f/8. Sharpness drops slightly at f/11, and it’s at f/16 where diffraction begins to soften the image overall. This increases further when you stop down to f/22. These latter apertures aren’t relevant to astrophotography; the medium ones aren’t either but the sharpness produced at f/1.8 and f/2.8 is exactly what you want. Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE: Design The Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE lens is compact but quite heavy. (Image credit: James Abbott) Weather-sealed build Compact yet heavy Great handling The 16mm f/1.8 lens is something of an oddity in one respect: it’s both compact and heavy considering its size, although this comes down to its optical construction. The lens weighs 19.4 oz (550 g) with a size of just 3.35 x 4.06 in (85.2 x 103 mm). It does, however, balance well with Sony A-series cameras. The 16mm f/1.8 is made up of 15 elements in 12 groups, including four ED glass and three aspherical lenses. The optical construction is designed to deliver sharpness, detail and high contrast with minimal distortion. It’s fair to say it achieves these. Of course, you will experience some perspective distortion when tilting the lens up to capture more of the night sky when there are ground elements in the foreground. Unlike some wide-angle lenses, the front element isn’t bulbous, and it features an HD nano multilayer coating with a water-resistant and antifouling coating. The filter thread is also just 77mm, so you can easily attach screw-in and square filters if you use them for your astrophotography. The minimum focusing distance of the lens is 10.6 inches (27 cm), which is great for landscape photographers but less important for astrophotographers. The color screen is great for night shooting. James Abbott The aperture ring can be set to click or clickless operation. James Abbott Main controls on the left side of the lens. James Abbott The all-metal body has a premium look and feel. James Abbott Build quality is impressive thanks to an all-metal body and weather-sealing. This gives the lens a premium look, and it feels robust in the hand. There’s also a useful digital color screen that displays lens information. When it comes to controls, there are possibly a few more on this lens than you might find on the average prime. There’s a manual focusing ring that’s wide enough for use when wearing gloves, a manual aperture ring that can be set to stepped and stepless operation using a switch on one side of the lens, two customizable Fn buttons and an AF/MF switch. Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE: Functionality The Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE is excellent for astrophotography. (Image credit: James Abbott) Small color digital screen Customizable Fn buttons 105.6-degree field of view The Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE is a full-frame lens offering a generous 105.6-degree field of view, allowing you to capture more of the night sky. This lens naturally works with all Sony FE bodies, and if you shoot APS-C, it will give you an equivalent focal length of 24mm. This means if you currently own an APS-C camera but plan to upgrade to full-frame, this lens could comfortably join you on that journey. As prime lenses go, this one has a few more bells and whistles than most, so there are a few more things to talk about than usual. Focusing is internal, so the front element doesn’t rotate or extend outwards, which is great when using filters. For astrophotography, manual focus is the only way to go, but this lens also has autofocus for when you’re shooting other subjects. The autofocus isn't the fastest we’ve seen, taking about 0.25 seconds to lock onto subjects when the lens is wide open, or 0.5 seconds when stopped down. This is driven by an SMT stepping motor, which is quiet but audible. One feature that you don’t see on many lenses is a small color digital screen on the top of the lens. This shows the focus distance, aperture setting and the active Fn control. Is it a gimmick? A bit. Is it useful? Yes. For astrophotography, the screen is definitely useful because it’s illuminated. As with most Viltrox lenses, there’s also a USB-C port on the lens mount so it can be powered. This allows you to connect the lens to the Viltrox Lens app via Bluetooth to update firmwa

item.title: UK’s rewards for North Sea drilling will be droughts, floods and fires
item.description: A protest against the UK government’s approval for drilling at the Jackdaw gas field, outside the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero in London TOLGA AKMEN/EPA/Shutterstock After months of vacillation, the UK government has finally announced that drilling will go ahead at the Jackdaw gas field in the North Sea. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has described the move as “a pragmatic approach”, saying “we’ll still require oil and gas as part of our energy needs for decades to come”. The thing is, the climate of our rapidly heating planet doesn’t recognise pragmatism. The only thing it acknowledges and responds to is how much carbon dioxide is added to the atmosphere, and it doesn’t care where it comes from. Read more The collapse of the AMOC would be catastrophic. How will we know when it’s coming? A study published two weeks ago reveals that the rate of global heating doubled over the period 2011 to 2025, compared with 1971 to 2025, so that the planet’s temperature is now rising at a rate of 0.4°C a decade. The corollary of this is that the 1.5°C limit is set to be permanently breached as soon as 2028 – a full decade sooner than previous projections. Furthermore, the speed of heating means that even the projected rise of 2.8°C by 2100 is now unrealistic, and points towards a much hotter world arriving far more quickly. Advertisement Nonetheless, a report published today by the UN Environmental Programme claims that, while the 1.5°C threshold is now dead in the water , it may still be possible to limit the global average temperature rise to just a few tenths of a degree above this. According to the report , to have a “good” chance of staying this side of 1.7°C to 1.8°C, greenhouse gas emissions would need to fall 18 per cent by the end of this decade, 45 per cent by 2035 and a whisker under 70 per cent by 2040. That “good” is doing some seriously heavy lifting, but what’s more, the idea that emissions, in the real world, will drop by more than two-thirds in less than 15 years is pure fantasy. Especially at a time when fossil fuel corporations are planning for expansion, aided and abetted by the governments of the UK, the US and others. Free newsletter Sign up to The Earth Edition Sign up to newsletter Instead, as pointed out by Johan Rockström, director of the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research in Germany, the implementation of current national commitments would mean global emissions reaching close to 50 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (a measure of the global warming potential of all greenhouse gases) by 2035. And that’s assuming that such commitments are adhered to, which is by no means certain as governments, including that of the UK, row back on green measures. Today’s decision to go ahead with Jackdaw, and to allow drilling in adjacent areas, is entirely the wrong one. A separate decision about the far more carbon-intensive Rosebank oil field is expected by the end of the year. Going ahead with either project guarante
item.dc:creator: Bill McGuire
item.content:encoded: A protest against the UK government’s approval for drilling at the Jackdaw gas field, outside the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero in London TOLGA AKMEN/EPA/Shutterstock After months of vacillation, the UK government has finally announced that drilling will go ahead at the Jackdaw gas field in the North Sea. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has described the move as “a pragmatic approach”, saying “we’ll still require oil and gas as part of our energy needs for decades to come”. The thing is, the climate of our rapidly heating planet doesn’t recognise pragmatism. The only thing it acknowledges and responds to is how much carbon dioxide is added to the atmosphere, and it doesn’t care where it comes from. Read more The collapse of the AMOC would be catastrophic. How will we know when it’s coming? A study published two weeks ago reveals that the rate of global heating doubled over the period 2011 to 2025, compared with 1971 to 2025, so that the planet’s temperature is now rising at a rate of 0.4°C a decade. The corollary of this is that the 1.5°C limit is set to be permanently breached as soon as 2028 – a full decade sooner than previous projections. Furthermore, the speed of heating means that even the projected rise of 2.8°C by 2100 is now unrealistic, and points towards a much hotter world arriving far more quickly. Advertisement Nonetheless, a report published today by the UN Environmental Programme claims that, while the 1.5°C threshold is now dead in the water , it may still be possible to limit the global average temperature rise to just a few tenths of a degree above this. According to the report , to have a “good” chance of staying this side of 1.7°C to 1.8°C, greenhouse gas emissions would need to fall 18 per cent by the end of this decade, 45 per cent by 2035 and a whisker under 70 per cent by 2040. That “good” is doing some seriously heavy lifting, but what’s more, the idea that emissions, in the real world, will drop by more than two-thirds in less than 15 years is pure fantasy. Especially at a time when fossil fuel corporations are planning for expansion, aided and abetted by the governments of the UK, the US and others. Free newsletter Sign up to The Earth Edition Sign up to newsletter Instead, as pointed out by Johan Rockström, director of the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research in Germany, the implementation of current national commitments would mean global emissions reaching close to 50 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (a measure of the global warming potential of all greenhouse gases) by 2035. And that’s assuming that such commitments are adhered to, which is by no means certain as governments, including that of the UK, row back on green measures. Today’s decision to go ahead with Jackdaw, and to allow drilling in adjacent areas, is entirely the wrong one. A separate decision about the far more carbon-intensive Rosebank oil field is expected by the end of the year. Going ahead with either project guarantees that the UK is now complicit in pushing up global greenhouse gas emissions, and reducing the chances of limiting the global average temperature rise to something more manageable. At the same time, the decision marks a conscious commitment to retain fossil fuel infrastructure and lock in hydrocarbons to the country’s energy mix for decades to come. Not only will this endanger national carbon reduction goals, but it will hand other nations an excuse to green-light their own new fossil fuel projects. Read more Can everyone live a ‘good life’ without destroying the planet? Every tonne of CO2 we don’t emit makes our future that little bit less grim, and every tonne we pump out takes fully 400,000 years to remove from the atmosphere completely. There is nothing pragmatic, then, about opening the North Sea to more drilling. The decision will go unrewarded in terms of cheaper energy and more jobs, but the resulting higher temperatures will ensure that the country is rewarded in the form of more drought, floods and wildfires.

item.title: Crimson Desert DLC Officially Confirms Huge New Features List
item.description: After Pearl Abyss announced a brief delay at the end of September for Crimson Desert 's upcoming DLC, Charting the Unknown is now just over one week from being released. While the developer has been steadily updating and streamlining the overwhelmingly large RPG since its release back in March, the game's first DLC marks an even more massive overhaul that brings much-needed fixes as well as more systems than most players will know what to do with. We had a general idea of what would be included in Charting the Unknown, but now Pearl Abyss has released a comprehensive feature list, and it is more ambitious than we could have expected.

item.title: 10 injured in Third Mainland Bridge crash, train collision averted
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni At least 10 passengers sustained injuries in a multiple-vehicle crash on the Third Mainland Bridge, Lagos, on Wednesday, while emergency responders averted a possible train collision at Ilupeju Bypass after a commercial bus broke down on a railway track. The Lagos State Emergency Management Agency (LASEMA) said the bridge accident occurred on Wednesday morning when a commercial bus stopped to repair a faulty tyre and was rammed by another bus. A trailer subsequently hit the second bus before fleeing the scene. According to the agency, emergency responders administered first aid to the injured passengers and evacuated them to hospital for treatment. The affected section of the bridge was later cleared and reopened to traffic. In a separate incident at Ilupeju Bypass, an emergency response team removed a broken-down commercial bus from a railway track with the aid of a light tow truck, averting a possible collision with an approaching train. The agency said emergency responders were on the ground to manage the situation. LASEMA urged motorists to avoid carrying out roadside repairs on highways and bridges, advising them to maintain their vehicles regularly to prevent accidents. It also urged residents requiring emergency assistance to call its emergency numbers, 767 or 112. The post 10 injured in Third Mainland Bridge crash, train collision averted appeared first on Vanguard News .
item.dc:creator: Nwafor
item.content:encoded: By Olasunkanmi Akoni At least 10 passengers sustained injuries in a multiple-vehicle crash on the Third Mainland Bridge, Lagos, on Wednesday, while emergency responders averted a possible train collision at Ilupeju Bypass after a commercial bus broke down on a railway track. The Lagos State Emergency Management Agency (LASEMA) said the bridge accident occurred on Wednesday morning when a commercial bus stopped to repair a faulty tyre and was rammed by another bus. A trailer subsequently hit the second bus before fleeing the scene. According to the agency, emergency responders administered first aid to the injured passengers and evacuated them to hospital for treatment. The affected section of the bridge was later cleared and reopened to traffic. In a separate incident at Ilupeju Bypass, an emergency response team removed a broken-down commercial bus from a railway track with the aid of a light tow truck, averting a possible collision with an approaching train. The agency said emergency responders were on the ground to manage the situation. LASEMA urged motorists to avoid carrying out roadside repairs on highways and bridges, advising them to maintain their vehicles regularly to prevent accidents. It also urged residents requiring emergency assistance to call its emergency numbers, 767 or 112. The post 10 injured in Third Mainland Bridge crash, train collision averted appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Pokémon Is Officially Planning a Big Retail Expansion in 2029

item.title: Iran says Egypt entering Yemen war makes situation ‘more difficult’
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Wednesday that any interference in the Yemen war by Egypt or any other country would make the situation “more difficult”. “Egypt has sufficient experience to avoid entangling itself in such a highly complex conflict,” said Iran’s top diplomat in an interview with Iraqi state broadcaster Al-Iraqiya aired on Tuesday. “We believe that any foreign presence or interference will only make resolving this issue more difficult,” Araghchi noted. He added that Egypt has said it “will not enter Yemen or engage in a war against Yemen”. The decade-plus war between the Iran-backed Houthis and a Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen’s internationally recognised government reignited in July. The Houthis seized much of Yemen’s Red Sea coastline in September and have since launched attacks on Saudi Arabia, including strikes on state oil giant Aramco and Riyadh’s international airport, where 13 people were killed on October 10. Egypt’s parliament on Monday delayed a debate on President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi’s request to authorise military support for Saudi Arabia until next week. Sisi had asked lawmakers to approve military support for Saudi Arabia if requested by the kingdom, which has come under near-daily attacks from Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis. Sisi said Egypt was not seeking to “confront or attack anyone”, adding: “We are speaking only about defence.” The post Iran says Egypt entering Yemen war makes situation ‘more difficult’ appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Reforms Are Yielding Results, Okpebholo Urges Edo Residents To Back Tinubu’s Re-Election
item.description: Edo State Governor, Monday Okpebholo, has appealed to residents of the state to support President Bola Tinubu’s administration, saying the federal government’s economic reforms are beginning to show in development and better governance. Okpebholo appealed on Wednesday when he visited the Ojuromi of Uromi, HRH Zaiki Anselm Aidenojie II, at the traditional ruler’s palace in Esan Northeast Local Government Area. He was accompanied by members of the All Progressives Congress (APC), according to a statement by Chief Press Secretary to Okpebholo, Dr. Patrick Ebojele. Edo State Governor, Monday Okpebholo, speaking on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, when he visited the Ojuromi of Uromi, HRH Zaiki Anselm Aidenojie II, at the traditional ruler’s palace, in Esan Northeast Local Government Area. Speaking on his administration’s record, the governor listed road construction, the upgrade of primary healthcare centers, regular payment of salaries, and the building of schools among the areas where work is ongoing. He admitted that much of what his government is doing will not show results overnight. “Most of the work I am undertaking can not manifest in one day. It takes time because it involves construction,” he said. “Many roads have been completed, and we have started several others in different parts of the state. They will ease movement and improve economic activities in Edo,” he said. Governor Okpebholo also spoke about electricity, one of the state’s long-standing challenges. He said a 100-megawatt power plant is expected to come on stream in Edo South in the near future, with another project to add 16 megawatts. “These projects are part of our efforts to address the power problem in the state,” he said. The governor credited the federal government for progress so far. “The man driving that success is Mr. President. That is why I am here to tell you that I do not want Edo to be in opposition to this government because of the progress we are already making,” he said. Earlier, His Royal Highness (HRH) Aidenojie II, Ojuromi of Uromi,speaking on behalf of the Esan Enigies commended the governor for his efforts at fast tracking development to the state. He prayed for God’s blessings and prayed that God would continue to give him wisdom to pilot the affairs of the state. Aidenojie, who described the governor as his son, assured him that the anticipated eight years of his administration would be completed. The post Reforms Are Yielding Results, Okpebholo Urges Edo Residents To Back Tinubu’s Re-Election appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Macron lands in Saudi Arabia on surprise ‘solidarity’ visit
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron landed in Riyadh where he is due to meet Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman on Wednesday, in a surprise “solidarity” visit after weeks of Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. Macron is the first Western leader to visit the kingdom since Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis intensified their attacks this month. The trip is part of a Gulf tour to secure diesel and petrol supplies as Macron seeks to bring down energy prices following violent protests in France sparked by rising living costs that have created a political crisis for the president. “The president of the republic is travelling to Saudi Arabia this afternoon to meet with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman,” a statement from Macron’s office said. The visit aimed to “demonstrate France’s solidarity with the kingdom in the face of the attacks carried out by the Houthis against its territory, and to continue efforts undertaken on securing and diversifying hydrocarbon supplies”, it added. In recent weeks, Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia have reached an unprecedented scale, forcing Riyadh airport to shut and the postponement of a major investment conference. A Houthi attempt to blockade Saudi ports is also hampering oil exports from the kingdom. AFP The post Macron lands in Saudi Arabia on surprise ‘solidarity’ visit appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: NDC rejects C’River chairman’s listing in APC campaign council
item.description: By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Cross River has rejected the listing of its state chairman, Goddie Akpama, in the purported All Progressives Congress (APC) State Campaign Council directory. The party made its position known in a statement by its State Publicity Secretary, Mr Cletus Amawu, and made available to Vanguard in Calabar on Wednesday. The NDC said an online directory had listed Akpama under the Chieftaincy Affairs category of the APC campaign council, describing the publication as misleading. It insisted that Akpama was neither a member of the APC nor affiliated with the party’s campaign council. The party also corrected the name displayed in the directory, saying his full and correct name was Goddie Archibong Akpama, not “Goddy Akpama”. According to the NDC, Akpama remains committed to his responsibilities as the party’s state chairman and continues to work towards advancing its political objectives. The party expressed concern that the listing could mislead the public, confuse political stakeholders, and undermine Akpama’s political standing. It urged those responsible for compiling, hosting, or circulating the directory to explain how his name was included, remove the listing, and issue a public clarification. The NDC also urged journalists, political stakeholders, and members of the public not to regard the listing as evidence of Akpama’s membership of the APC. The party said Akpama’s political activities remained within the NDC, adding that political disagreements should be resolved through legitimate engagement rather than the circulation of misleading information. It reiterated its demand for the immediate removal of the listing and a public clarification from those responsible. Amawu reaffirmed that Akpama remained focused on his political responsibilities under the NDC platform and would not be distracted by what the party described as attempts to misrepresent his political affiliation. The post NDC rejects C’River chairman’s listing in APC campaign council appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Senate mourns former Delta State Governor Uduaghan
item.description: Urges Delta State Government to preserve the records of significant public programmes and development initiatives undertaken during his administration By Henry Umoru ABUJA- THE Senate has mourned the death of former Governor of Delta State, Dr. Emmanuel Uduaghan who died just three days before his 72nd birthday, according to his family. The Upper Chamber has commiserated with the Uduaghan family, the Itsekiri nation, the Government and people of Delta State, and all those affected by his passing, just as it conveyed its condolence to the family, Government and people of Delta State. The Senate has urged the Government of Delta State to preserve the records of significant public programmes and development initiatives undertaken during his administration, as part of the State’s institutional and developmental history. Resolutions of the Senate on Wednesday were sequel to a motion titled “Demise of His Excellency, Dr. Emmanuel Eweta Uduaghan, CON, Former Governor of Delta State (2007-2015).” It was sponsored by Senator Joel Onowakpo Thomas, APC, Delta South and co- sponsored by Senator Ned Nwoko, APC, Delta North; Senator Ede Dafinone, APC, Delta Central and Senator Senator Natasha Akpoti-Uduaghan, PDP, Kogi Central. The Senate observed a minute of silence in honour of the late Dr. Emmanuel Eweta Uduaghan, CON, in recognition of his years of service to Delta State and the Nigerian nation. The Upper Chamber prayed Almighty God to grant his soul eternal rest and give his family, friends and the people of Delta State the fortitude to bear this irreparable loss. Earlier in his presentation, Senator Joel Onowakpo Thomas said that “The Senate:Notes with profound grief and a deep sense of loss the passing of His Excellency, Dr. Emmanuel Eweta Uduaghan, CON, former Governor of Delta State, distinguished medical practitioner, -statesman and public servant, who passed away on 19 October 2026, leaving behind a legacy of service to humanity and significant contributions to the political, social and economic development of Delta State; “Recalls that Dr. Uduaghan was born on 22 October 1954 in Abigborodo, Warri North Local Government Area of Delta State, and trained as a medical doctor at the University of Benin, where he obtained his Bachelor of Medicine and Bachelor of Surgery degree, subsequently pursuing a professional career in medicine before venturing into public administration; “Also recalls that his public service career commenced at the executive level when he was appointed Commissioner for Health in Delta State in 1999, a position he held until 2003, before serving as Secretary to the Delta State Government from 2003 to 2007, and subsequently as Governor of Delta State from 29 May 2007 to 29 May 2015; “Acknowledges that his professional background in medicine profoundly influenced his approach to governance, particularly his emphasis on healthcare delivery, human welfare and the expansion of access to essential medical services for vulnerable segments

item.content:encoded: Urges Delta State Government to preserve the records of significant public programmes and development initiatives undertaken during his administration By Henry Umoru ABUJA- THE Senate has mourned the death of former Governor of Delta State, Dr. Emmanuel Uduaghan who died just three days before his 72nd birthday, according to his family. The Upper Chamber has commiserated with the Uduaghan family, the Itsekiri nation, the Government and people of Delta State, and all those affected by his passing, just as it conveyed its condolence to the family, Government and people of Delta State. The Senate has urged the Government of Delta State to preserve the records of significant public programmes and development initiatives undertaken during his administration, as part of the State’s institutional and developmental history. Resolutions of the Senate on Wednesday were sequel to a motion titled “Demise of His Excellency, Dr. Emmanuel Eweta Uduaghan, CON, Former Governor of Delta State (2007-2015).” It was sponsored by Senator Joel Onowakpo Thomas, APC, Delta South and co- sponsored by Senator Ned Nwoko, APC, Delta North; Senator Ede Dafinone, APC, Delta Central and Senator Senator Natasha Akpoti-Uduaghan, PDP, Kogi Central. The Senate observed a minute of silence in honour of the late Dr. Emmanuel Eweta Uduaghan, CON, in recognition of his years of service to Delta State and the Nigerian nation. The Upper Chamber prayed Almighty God to grant his soul eternal rest and give his family, friends and the people of Delta State the fortitude to bear this irreparable loss. Earlier in his presentation, Senator Joel Onowakpo Thomas said that “The Senate:Notes with profound grief and a deep sense of loss the passing of His Excellency, Dr. Emmanuel Eweta Uduaghan, CON, former Governor of Delta State, distinguished medical practitioner, -statesman and public servant, who passed away on 19 October 2026, leaving behind a legacy of service to humanity and significant contributions to the political, social and economic development of Delta State; “Recalls that Dr. Uduaghan was born on 22 October 1954 in Abigborodo, Warri North Local Government Area of Delta State, and trained as a medical doctor at the University of Benin, where he obtained his Bachelor of Medicine and Bachelor of Surgery degree, subsequently pursuing a professional career in medicine before venturing into public administration; “Also recalls that his public service career commenced at the executive level when he was appointed Commissioner for Health in Delta State in 1999, a position he held until 2003, before serving as Secretary to the Delta State Government from 2003 to 2007, and subsequently as Governor of Delta State from 29 May 2007 to 29 May 2015; “Acknowledges that his professional background in medicine profoundly influenced his approach to governance, particularly his emphasis on healthcare delivery, human welfare and the expansion of access to essential medical services for vulnerable segments of the population; “Recognizes that one of the defining features of his administration was the introduction and implementation of free maternal healthcare and under-five healthcare programmes, aimed at reducing the financial burden of medical treatment on pregnant women, nursing mothers and young children, thereby promoting maternal and child health and improving access to essential healthcare services; “Also recognizes his administration’s efforts to strengthen tertiary healthcare through the development of the Delta State University Teaching Hospital at Oghara, including investments in medical infrastructure, specialised services and institutional capacity, with a view to expanding access to advanced medical treatment within the State and reducing the need for patients to seek certain specialised services outside the country; “Notes that these healthcare initiatives reflected his conviction that the wellbeing of citizens constitutes a fundamental responsibility of government and that public investment in preventive, maternal, child and specialised healthcare is essential to human development, “Acknowledges that his administration pursued an extensive programme of educational development, including the rehabilitation and remodelling of public primary and secondary schools, the construction and renovation of classrooms, the improvement of school facilities and the expansion of educational opportunities for children and young people across the State, “Also acknowledges the introduction of educational support initiatives, including the EDUMARSHAL programme aimed at encouraging school attendance, efforts to reduce the burden of school-related fees and levies, support for public examination costs and scholarship opportunities for academically outstanding students, thereby promoting access to education and investing in the future workforce of Delta State, “Observes that these educational interventions were underpinned by the recognition that sustainable development requires not merely the provision of physical infrastructure but also the cultivation of knowledge, skills, innovation and human capital necessary for economic growth and social advancement.” According to him, the Senate “Recognizes that infrastructural development constituted a major priority of his administration, particularly through road construction and rehabilitation, improvements in transportation infrastructure and the development of Asaba International Airport, which was conceived to enhance connectivity, facilitate the movement of people and goods, promote commercial activities and strengthen the position of Delta State as an important economic destination; “Also recognizes that his administration pursued improvements in other transport facilities, including the expansion and upgrading of existing aviation infrastructure, as part of a broader strategy to improve mobility, stimulate investment and support economic activities within the State; “Acknowledges his Delta Beyond Oil agenda, which sought to reduce Delta State’s traditional dependence on crude oil revenue through the promotion of agriculture, tourism, small and medium-scale enterprises, investment and other productive sectors of the economy, with the objective of building a more diversified, resilient and sustainable economic base for present and future generations; “Notes that the Delta Beyond Oil vision reflected an important development principle: that the wealth derived from natural resources must be translated into lasting economic opportunities, productive capacity, employment and improved living standards, rather than leave the State excessively vulnerable to fluctuations in oil revenue; “Further acknowledges his administration’s emphasis on youth empowerment and the development of sporting talent, recognising sport as an instrument of discipline, opportunity, social integration and national pride, “Observes that under his leadership, Team Delta emerged overall champion at the 2009 National Sports Festival in Kaduna and again at the 2012 National Sports Festival in Lagos, while finishing second at the 2011 edition hosted by Rivers State, achievements which reinforced Delta State’s reputation as one of Nigeria’s leading centres of sporting excellence, “Further notes that his administration supported sporting development through incentives for athletes, the promotion of grassroots participation and the strengthening of sports administration, thereby creating opportunities for young people to develop their talents and represent the State at national and other competitive levels; “Recognises that his administration operated during a challenging period in the Niger Delta, characterised by militancy, insecurity, disruptions to economic activities and longstanding grievances relating to resource control, environmental degradation and community development, “Acknowledges his efforts to promote peace, reconciliation and stability through dialogue and sustaine

item.title: ‘The audience gets to be in on it’: How narrative-led gameplay is Call of Duty’s greatest weapon
item.description: As video games chase spectacle, Modern Warfare 4 makes a case for putting character and consequence at the heart of its biggest battles • Don’t get Pushing Buttons delivered to your inbox? Sign up here In these strange, subdued weeks before the much-anticipated release of Grand Theft Auto VI, there have still been some welcome surprises. Onimusha: Way of the Sword revived a half-forgotten samurai action series with much aplomb, while Silent Hill: Townfall transported all of the franchise’s bloody, dread-filled psychological horror to … the picturesque Scottish coast. Even more shocking to games writers , though, is the fact that the forthcoming Modern Warfare 4 has one of the best Call of Duty campaign modes for at least six years – and might even be up there with the original Modern Warfare trilogy. The setting is an invasion of South Korea by its northern neighbour – a setup that could have fuelled a hundred instantly forgettable Netflix films, but has proved controversial in a video game. The authoritarian regime has a new (fictitious) ruler and a powerful experimental weapon, which it’s not afraid to use as the opening gambit in an explosive attack. You take on the role of Park Hyun Jun, a conscripted South Korean soldier who, along with his small unit of similarly inexperienced grunts, gets caught in the firestorm as cities burn and enemy paratroopers fill the skies. Continue reading...

item.title: The best Kindles in the UK for every bookworm and budget – tested
item.description: Whether you want a colour screen, somewhere to scribble notes or a child-friendly model, here’s what we recommend from Amazon’s e-reader range • The best e-readers From that fresh paperback smell to the wrinkles in the spine, nothing beats a real book. But if you’re sick of the space they take up in your home, or the weight they steal from your holiday luggage allowance, it might be worth considering an Amazon Kindle. It can fit thousands of weighty reads into as little as 158g, and as tech goes, it’s almost immune to the sort of pathological time-wasting features that come with modern phones and tablets. Amazon Kindles have been available in the UK for more than 15 years, so they’re an old-school gadget at this point. But in 2024, the biggest update yet arrived: colour, which added an important extra option to the existing Kindle lineup, alongside readers for children, for note-taking and for tighter budgets. Continue reading...

item.title: Stranger Than Heaven May Have Forgotten One Thing That Made Yakuza Great
item.description: I’m from the Bay Area, so I was especially excited to experience RGG’s riff on old-timey San Francisco in the prologue. Turns out, it’s not an explorable area, and the buildings and narrow alleyways had more of a generic East Coast feeling to me. Given how vividly this studio has captured real-world neighborhoods like Waikiki, Kabukicho, and Dotonbori in previous games, I was hoping for more, especially given the time period. (There was an extremely elaborate World’s Fair in San Francisco in 1915!) There’s certainly a lot of fog and it looks miserably cold at night, so at least that part is accurate.

(There was an extremely elaborate World’s Fair in San Francisco in 1915!) There’s certainly a lot of fog and it looks miserably cold at night, so at least that part is accurate.

item.title: See Inside Cells Like Never Before in These Vivid Microscopic Images
item.description: On a frigid February morning in Edinburgh, Scotland, Patrick Hickey had run out of living things to put under his microscope. The plants and fungi in his garden had dried up, and summer puddles, with their flamboyant biological complexity, had long frozen over. Hickey, a mycologist at Hypha Research Ltd., was using plant leaves to study mitochondria, cellular organelles that generate energy. Source

item.title: Space botanist conducts plant experiments in orbit | Space photo of the day for Oct. 21, 2026
item.description: null NASA astronaut Luke Delaney conducts botany experiments on the ISS. (Image credit: NASA/Jessica Watkins) Growing plants in space? Yes indeed! NASA astronauts are conducting botany experiments aboard the International Space Station (ISS). What is it? In this snapshot — captured by NASA astronaut Jessica Watkins, commander of SpaceX 's Crew-13 mission to the ISS — we can see fellow NASA spaceflyer Luke Delaney hard at work aboard the ISS. And while he's orbiting around our planet aboard a laboratory in the vacuum of space, he's also growing plants. In the photo, Delaney is working petri dishes and experiment modules that support our growing understanding of how plants grow in the microgravity environment aboard the station. Specifically, the experiments Delaney is working on will investigate the genetic responses of plants in this environment. This is not the first time that researchers have studied plants in space. In fact, ISS astronauts have conducted a wide variety of plant experiments and investigations over the years. They've grown peppers and other edible produce and even proved that moss can survive outside the station, in the harsh environment of space. Why is it incredible? When you picture the inside of an orbiting space station, you might imagine the white and gray walls with computers, buttons, switches and other such tech speckling the scene. But the space station is also full of (non-astronaut) life, thanks to the incredible variety of biological experiments onboard. While space is "the final frontier," and we look outward to study everything from black holes to exploding stars, outer space can also help teach us about own planet. Satellites look back at Earth, studying its changing landforms, migrating wildlife, diminishing glaciers and natural disasters. Onboard the ISS, astronauts conduct experiments with plants, animals, microscopic organisms and an incredible amount of studies supporting human health and medical care. While space might be the final frontier, so much of the work done in space is designed to benefit us back here on Earth .

item.title: ‘A complete threat’: Rio Ngumoha’s electric display excites Van Dijk and Liverpool
item.description: Teenager produced man-of-the-match performance against Villarreal and has learned from Salah, says Reds captain The shot sailed wide of Peter Gulacsi’s top corner and into the Kop, affording Villarreal much-needed respite at 4-2, but for Andoni Iraola it was a standout moment in a scintillating Champions League display from Rio Ngumoha. To a coach that called for versatility from all of his wingers this summer, here was a significant step forward among many from the 18-year-old at Anfield. There were questions over how Ngumoha would adapt to playing on the right even before Liverpool increased the likelihood by signing Bradley Barcola for £123m from Paris Saint-Germain. On his fifth start under Iraola on Tuesday, which his side ultimately won 4-3 , Liverpool witnessed an answer: quickly, incisively and confidently. The teenager’s willingness to cut inside from the right and shoot from distance with the left foot captured Iraola’s imagination as much as the devastating run that created Alexis Mac Allister’s second goal of the game. Continue reading...

item.title: OpenAI says an AI agent lied about disabling its safety monitoring system
item.description: OpenAI disclosed a pair of safety incidents that involved AI agents weakening their safety monitoring systems during internal coding tasks. In one incident, OpenAI says its GPT-6 Astra agent disabled its safety monitor when copying reference code - and then lied about it. "The reference didn't configure a monitor, and Astra decided that was reason to remove the monitoring integration from the user's code," Marcus Williams, an AI safety researcher at OpenAI, writes on X . "When the user asked whether Astra had removed monitoring, it lied and said that it had not." item.title: Now Serato DJ works on your iPhone
item.description: Serato DJ for iOS is finally bringing the company's pro-level DJ suite to the iPhone and iPad . Until now, the company had only dipped its toes into mobile software, with apps like Pyro that basically just added some autofades between songs in a playlist. This is the first time most of the features of its flagship DJ app are available on a mobile device, even though competitors like Rekordbox and Algoriddim have had proper mobile DJ apps for some time. If you're a DJ used to Serato on a laptop, the workflow should feel instantly familiar. You can even transfer your library directly from Serato DJ 5.0 on your laptop to your iOS device either … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: How To Protect Yourself From Ebola Infection
item.description: The Federal Government on Tuesday confirmed the first case of the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). Ebola is a disease that spreads through direct contact with the blood or bodily fluids of an infected person or animal, according to the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC). ﻿ Following the confirmation, below are facts on transmission/causes, symptoms, and how to protect yourself and loved ones. How Does It Spread? Ebola can be spread through: Direct contact with blood, sweat, saliva, vomit, or other bodily fluids of an infected, symptomatic person Touching contaminated surfaces such as clothing, bedding, or other materials contaminated with fluids from an infected individual Consuming infected wild animals, handling deceased bodies without safety gear. Know The Symptoms Symptoms typically appear two to 21 days after exposure. The symptoms include: Fever Vomitting Headache Diarrhea Weakness/Fatigue Bleeding Muscle pain Sore throat How To Protect Yourself Wash hands regularly with clean running water and soap, or use alcohol-based sanitiser. Avoid contact with dead bodies and wild animals. Ensure all meat products are handled hygienically and thoroughly cooked. Do not touch bodily fluids of sick individuals or handle deceased bodies without professional health protocols. Health workers should adhere strictly to Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) standards. Myth Vs Facts Let’s set the record straight! Myth: Ebola spreads via casual contact (handshake, hugging). Fact: Ebola does not spread through casual contact. It requires direct contact with the bodily fluids of an infected person. Myth: Ebola spreads through food and water. Fact: Ebola does not spread through food and water, but all foods should be thoroughly cooked. Drink clean water always. Myth: Ebola spreads through the air. Fact: Ebola is not an airborne virus. Transmission strictly requires direct physical contact with bodily fluids or contaminated objects from a person showing active symptoms. Myth: Healthcare facilities are not safe during outbreaks. Fact: Healthcare facilities are strengthening infection prevention and control measures, including triage systems, hand hygiene, use of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), and isolation procedures to protect patients and healthcare workers. Stay informed and avoid panic. Spreading unverified rumours causes unnecessary fear and hampers response efforts. Always rely on official health updates. The post How To Protect Yourself From Ebola Infection appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Real reasons Defence Chief, Gen. Oluyede was honoured in Abuja
item.description: Fresh facts have emerged on the reasons General Olufemi Olatunbosun Oluyede, the present Chief of Defence Staff (CDS), was honoured by a set of reputable journalists at a conference that was held in Abuja recently. Apart from factors revealed by the organisers of the conference, checks showed that Gen. Oluyede’s recent sterling performance after his resolve to restore peace in the Northern region of the country earned him the laudable feat. At the well-attended conference that was held at the Army Command Officers’ Mess 1, located at Asokoro, Abuja, the organisers, under the aegis of Defence Correspondents Association of Nigeria (DECAN) explained that a lot successes under General Oluyede’s leadership have been documented. According to Odita Sunday, the leader of DECAN, an association of journalists covering defence and security issues in Nigeria, Gen. Oluyede’s leadership in ensuring jointness among the three services and his commitment to strengthening joint military operations is topnotch. The award to Oluyede highlights the importance of strategic military leadership, inter-service cooperation and constructive military-civilian engagement in advancing Nigeria’s security objectives. Here are some of the General Oluyede’s recorded successes that earned him a prestigious honour: Whole-of-government approach to national security Specifically, the award recognised his leadership in coordinating the operations of the Nigerian Army, Nigerian Navy and Nigerian Air Force towards addressing the country’s evolving security challenges. His leadership approach, according to the DECAN head, aligns with his military strategic philosophy of consolidating the capabilities of the Armed Forces of Nigeria through enhanced jointness, improved operational posture, personnel welfare and sound administration. Sunday said the philosophy also emphasises a whole-of-government approach to national security, recognising the importance of collaboration among the military, other security agencies and relevant government institutions. Under Oluyede’s leadership, enhanced cooperation among the services remains central to efforts to improve operational effectiveness and respond to complex threats across Nigeria’s security theatres. item.content:encoded: Fresh facts have emerged on the reasons General Olufemi Olatunbosun Oluyede, the present Chief of Defence Staff (CDS), was honoured by a set of reputable journalists at a conference that was held in Abuja recently. Apart from factors revealed by the organisers of the conference, checks showed that Gen. Oluyede’s recent sterling performance after his resolve to restore peace in the Northern region of the country earned him the laudable feat. At the well-attended conference that was held at the Army Command Officers’ Mess 1, located at Asokoro, Abuja, the organisers, under the aegis of Defence Correspondents Association of Nigeria (DECAN) explained that a lot successes under General Oluyede’s leadership have been documented. According to Odita Sunday, the leader of DECAN, an association of journalists covering defence and security issues in Nigeria, Gen. Oluyede’s leadership in ensuring jointness among the three services and his commitment to strengthening joint military operations is topnotch. The award to Oluyede highlights the importance of strategic military leadership, inter-service cooperation and constructive military-civilian engagement in advancing Nigeria’s security objectives. Here are some of the General Oluyede’s recorded successes that earned him a prestigious honour: Whole-of-government approach to national security Specifically, the award recognised his leadership in coordinating the operations of the Nigerian Army, Nigerian Navy and Nigerian Air Force towards addressing the country’s evolving security challenges. His leadership approach, according to the DECAN head, aligns with his military strategic philosophy of consolidating the capabilities of the Armed Forces of Nigeria through enhanced jointness, improved operational posture, personnel welfare and sound administration. Sunday said the philosophy also emphasises a whole-of-government approach to national security, recognising the importance of collaboration among the military, other security agencies and relevant government institutions. Under Oluyede’s leadership, enhanced cooperation among the services remains central to efforts to improve operational effectiveness and respond to complex threats across Nigeria’s security theatres. The CDS’ emphasis on jointness, seeks to promote coordinated planning, intelligence sharing and the effective deployment of military capabilities, rather than allowing individual services to operate in isolation. Troops’ better welfare and restoration of peace in North Similarly, the military chief has been matching his words with actions, where he has stressed the importance of personnel welfare and professional development in building a motivated and effective fighting force. The approach recognises that operational success depends not only on equipment and combat capability but also on the professionalism, morale and welfare of the personnel entrusted with defending the country. The CDS noted that contemporary conflicts increasingly required technological superiority, timely intelligence and effective management of the information environment, alongside conventional military operations. Several frontline troops, who spoke to Daily Trust had confirmed that their welfare has improved in recent times, and that their morale is very high to perform their constitutional duties. Against this background, the troops attached with different theatres of operations have continued to rescue kidnapped victims across 19 Northern States and some places in the Southern part of the country. Official data obtained from the Directorate of Defence Media Operations, being headed by Major-General Michael Onoja, revealed that at least 3,500 civilians were rescued between January and September 2026. Under the same period, no fewer than 1,773 terrorists disturbing some places in the Northeast, North West, North Central and a few other places in the South were neutralised while 569 terrorists surrendered after feeling the heat. Military deepens rescue operations in North as 27 victims freed in Katsina Neither relenting nor resting on its oars, troops of the Nigerian military attached with Joint Task Force North West, Operation FANSAN YAMMA, recorded another operational success with the rescue of 27 kidnapped victims and recovery of a motorcycle in Katsina State. Providing details on how the victims were rescued, Major-General Onoja explained that on 16th October, 2026, troops of Sector 1 received a distress call on terrorist activities in Gamji community, Sabuwa Local Government Area. According to him, the terrorists had abducted 27 residents, comprising 15 males and 12 females but troops responded swiftly and pursued the terrorists until they were rescued while some of the abductors were neutralised. “Troops responded swiftly, pursuing the terrorists along the Gangare–Kamba axis. On contact, troops engaged with superior firepower, forcing the terrorists to abandon their victims and flee in disarray,” he said. He stated that all 27 victims were rescued unharmed during exploitation of the area, adding that they have been profiled and handed over to community leaders for reunification with their families. In a separate operation on the same day, troops conducting a fighting patrol around Kurba village in Kankara Local Government Area encountered terrorists on three motorcycles. “The terrorists fled on sighting troops, abandoning one motorcycle,” the senior military officer added. He noted that the successful operations underscore the sustained offensive posture and operational effectiveness of troops of Operation FANSAN YAMMA in denying terrorists freedom of action and safeguarding vulnerable communities across the Joint Operations Area. General Oluyede, who commended the troops for their gallantry, assured residents of Katsina, Zamfara and adjoining states of the unwavering commitment to restoring lasting peace and security. 103 terrorists neutralized in 8 days Meanwhile, no fewer than 103 terrorists have been neutralised within eight days while their several logistics hubs and storage facilities in the North East were also destroyed. Specifically, the terrorists were neutralised between October 10 and 18, 2026 during coordinated airstrikes and intelligence-led operations by the air and ground troops attached with the Operation Hadin Kai. The military high command, while confirming the development, said the operations targeted Boko Haram and Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) fighters, leadership structures and logistics networks in Borno and Adamawa states. It said the air component recorded a major success on October 18, when it conducted a precision strike on the alternative residence of Abu Saleem, the ISWAP Wali of South Lake Chad, in the Arina Woje area of Monguno Local Government Area (LGA), Borno State. According to the Defence Headquarters (DHQ), the sustained air campaign involved seven strikes against terrorist targets during the period. The DHQ said intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance activities underpinned the operation, while subsequent human intelligence confirmed the killing of Jindullah, a prominent ISWAP fighter who reportedly served as Abu Saleem’s chief security guard. Military airstrikes bomb ISWAP security chief, Shura Council member In the meantime, the military also confirmed the killing of Jindullah, who was identified as ISWAP’s Chief Security Guard and Abul Kissa, a member of the group’s Shura Council, alongside other prominent fighters in an airstrike in the Lake Chad region. The strike, conducted under the Joint Task Force, Operation Hadin Kai (OPHK), also destroyed logistical assets, including boat engines and motorcycles believed to have been used by the terrorists for movement and operational activities. According to preliminary post-strike assessments, indications emerged that the two operatives, identified as Jindullah and Abul Kissa, were among several fighters neutralised during the

item.title: Ebola: We Have A Problem With Delayed Diagnosis, Resources To Cope — Medical Doctor
item.description: Delayed diagnosis and a dearth of essential medical resources continue to hinder Nigeria’s public health response more than the nature of the Ebola virus, a professor at the College of Medicine, University of Lagos, Dr. Alero Roberts, has said. ﻿ Roberts explained that the pathogen’s behaviour remains unchanged and predictable, adding that the real problem lies in systemic shortcomings and hesitation by members of the public, which she said compromises patient outcomes before medical intervention can begin. “I have no problem with the virus itself; the virus is doing what the virus does, it hasn’t changed its behaviour, and the virus is doing what the virus does,.” she said during an interview on Channel Television’s The Morning Brief on Wednesday, while reacting to Nigeria’s first confirmed case of the Bundibugyo strain of he virus. “We do have problems with the delayed diagnosis, seeking appropriate care and definitely with the availability of resources to cope.” The doctor also noted that no country in the world has the resources to manage the massive outbreak of the virus. “No country in the world today has the resources to cope with the massive outbreak of Ebola. Once the diagnosis has been made, Ebola becomes a nursing care issue, and there are just not enough nurses; kudos to the nurses, there are just not enough nurses to cope with the major outbreak of Ebola,” Roberts said. “Which is what we are seeing in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) already, so we must stick with prevention, border control, identifying, and as a public health physician I will be going with high index of suspicion to treat every patient as a possible case and initiate what we call the IPC ring. “The IPC ring is Infection Prevention and Control; we have got to initiate that because those are our first line of defense and they have proven very effective in the past,” she added. Speaking further on the breakfast show, Roberts said, “If you have been exposed but you do not have any symptoms, the good thing about Ebola is that you are not contagious. Ebola is a direct transmission disease, unlike COVID, which was airborne, so you need to have contact with the bodily fluid of a patient who is exhibiting symptoms already”. She, however, noted that the 44 contacts with the patients are concerning but not an immediate danger. “So the fact that there are 44 contacts, although that is very concerning, it doesn’t pose an immediate danger to the public if none of those contacts have developed symptoms,” she added. The Federal Government on Tuesday said the virus was detected in a woman in FCT, Abuja, describing her as one who returned to Nigeria from Uganda with symptoms of the virus on October 7, the first in 12 years after the massive outbreak of the virus in Nigeria in 2014. The patient was said to have been in contact with 44 people, and all of them were said to be under close monitoring for signs of symptoms. The post Ebola: We Have A Problem With Delayed Diagnosis, Re

She, however, noted that the 44 contacts with the patients are concerning but not an immediate danger. “So the fact that there are 44 contacts, although that is very concerning, it doesn’t pose an immediate danger to the public if none of those contacts have developed symptoms,” she added. The Federal Government on Tuesday said the virus was detected in a woman in FCT, Abuja, describing her as one who returned to Nigeria from Uganda with symptoms of the virus on October 7, the first in 12 years after the massive outbreak of the virus in Nigeria in 2014. The patient was said to have been in contact with 44 people, and all of them were said to be under close monitoring for signs of symptoms. The post Ebola: We Have A Problem With Delayed Diagnosis, Resources To Cope — Medical Doctor appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: OneDrive gives Macs a million things to keep in sync
item.description: Microsoft is raising OneDrive's supported macOS sync limit to one million items, matching Windows, alongside new Copilot features, sharing controls, and an admin command-line tool. The macOS preview is scheduled for the Insiders ring this month, with general availability targeted for June 2027. Eligible devices must meet hardware and configuration requirements; others retain the existing 300,000-item supported limit. "This increase is intended to help organizations with large OneDrive and SharePoint libraries sync more content reliably across devices," Microsoft said. However, sync performance may suffer for large numbers of read-only files or accounts under legal hold. "We are actively working to improve performance and reliability for these scenarios," Microsoft said. Microsoft's cull of OneDrive's File Explorer shortcuts wasn't a retreat from AI. Its latest announcement gives Copilot more to do. The assistant can now be asked to analyze across files (for example, selecting several spreadsheets and getting the bot to come up with charts and graphs), told to organize folders, or save a repeated workflow as a personal skill in a Markdown file. There is also a Prompt Gallery to save the user from having to come up with their own ideas. Perhaps most interesting is the addition of "Hero Links," designed to end the proliferation of links to files and folders in OneDrive as permission needs change. The feature provides one link per file and folder by default, with permissions that can be updated while keeping the same URL. Automatic expiration controls are still coming, however. Organizations that require time-limited access will want to check that gap before adopting the feature. Administrators also get a OneDrive Sync command-line tool, available in private preview, for inspecting accounts, configuration, policies, and sync status. The tool can pull information from the OneDrive sync client and provide data on status, policy troubleshooting, and issue diagnosis, from folder backup and policy problems on a single PC to identifying devices that need attention across an organization. And yes, there is, of course, integration with AI agents. ®

item.title: Nvidia’s latest GPU driver brings a new way to speed up PC games
item.description: Nvidia is rolling out a new GPU driver today (621.01) that enables Microsoft's new Advanced Shader Delivery technology to speed up game launches. The technology also removes mid-game "just-in-time" shader compilation, reducing stuttering and CPU spikes. Microsoft's Advanced Shader Delivery works by offloading shader compilation for different hardware combinations to the cloud. item.title: When will SpaceX and Blue Origin fly to the moon? NASA reveals lunar lander timelines (and an Artemis III update)
item.description: null NASA has revealed new details about its plans to return astronauts to the surface of the moon, outlining a series of upcoming milestones for SpaceX and Blue Origin as both companies race to ready their lunar landers for the agency's Artemis program . During an Oct. 5 presentation at the Astronautical Congress (IAC) in Antalya, Türkiye, Steve Creech, acting manager of NASA's Human Landing System (HLS) Program, laid out development timelines for both spacecraft, with key demonstrations planned through early 2028 that include orbital refueling and uncrewed lunar landing tests to qualify the vehicles to fly astronauts to the surface of the moon . A more pressing deadline, however, is NASA's Artemis III mission, which is targeted for the third quarter (Q3) of 2027. Artemis III will launch four astronauts aboard NASA's Orion spacecraft to low Earth orbit (LEO), where they will rendezvous and dock with test versions of both companies' landers for interoperability checkouts. Those demonstrations will help inform NASA's determination about which lander the agency will choose to carry astronauts to the moon's surface on Artemis IV, targeted for early 2028. SpaceX and Blue Origin were both awarded NASA contracts to develop HLS vehicles — Starship and Blue Moon , respectively — and have spent the past several years refining their respective lunar lander designs and dealing with various delays along the way. In the face of those delays, and in an effort to better structure its mission progression for success, NASA overhauled its Artemis program architecture in February to maintain its goal of landing astronauts on the moon by the end of 2028 and establish a more regular cadence of uncrewed landings in the meantime. As part of that shakeup, Artemis III, previously the program's first crewed lunar landing mission, was moved up a year and repurposed for the lunar lander vehicle tests the agency is preparing to fly to LEO next year. The program's first moon landing remains scheduled for 2028, but was shifted to the manifest for Artemis IV. Between now and then, both SpaceX and Blue Origin have more than a dozen test demonstrations and vehicle milestones to achieve, including success during Artemis III and flights afterward. This will all lead up to a key decision NASA must make: Which vehicle will carry out the first crewed landing on the surface of the moon since the Apollo program ended in 1972? Starship reached for the first time on its most recent test flight, which occurred on Sept. 28 from SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas. NASA lists several other important goals for the vehicle to achieve in 2026, including (in the order listed during the IAC presentation) the first return and catch of the rocket's upgraded Version 3 (V3) booster at its launch pad; the first-ever return and catch of a Ship upper stage; the first Starship launch from one of SpaceX's launch pads still under construction on Florida's Space Coast; and, possibly, the first V3 booster
item.dc:creator: Josh Dinner
item.content:encoded: null NASA has revealed new details about its plans to return astronauts to the surface of the moon, outlining a series of upcoming milestones for SpaceX and Blue Origin as both companies race to ready their lunar landers for the agency's Artemis program . During an Oct. 5 presentation at the Astronautical Congress (IAC) in Antalya, Türkiye, Steve Creech, acting manager of NASA's Human Landing System (HLS) Program, laid out development timelines for both spacecraft, with key demonstrations planned through early 2028 that include orbital refueling and uncrewed lunar landing tests to qualify the vehicles to fly astronauts to the surface of the moon . A more pressing deadline, however, is NASA's Artemis III mission, which is targeted for the third quarter (Q3) of 2027. Artemis III will launch four astronauts aboard NASA's Orion spacecraft to low Earth orbit (LEO), where they will rendezvous and dock with test versions of both companies' landers for interoperability checkouts. Those demonstrations will help inform NASA's determination about which lander the agency will choose to carry astronauts to the moon's surface on Artemis IV, targeted for early 2028. SpaceX and Blue Origin were both awarded NASA contracts to develop HLS vehicles — Starship and Blue Moon , respectively — and have spent the past several years refining their respective lunar lander designs and dealing with various delays along the way. In the face of those delays, and in an effort to better structure its mission progression for success, NASA overhauled its Artemis program architecture in February to maintain its goal of landing astronauts on the moon by the end of 2028 and establish a more regular cadence of uncrewed landings in the meantime. As part of that shakeup, Artemis III, previously the program's first crewed lunar landing mission, was moved up a year and repurposed for the lunar lander vehicle tests the agency is preparing to fly to LEO next year. The program's first moon landing remains scheduled for 2028, but was shifted to the manifest for Artemis IV. Between now and then, both SpaceX and Blue Origin have more than a dozen test demonstrations and vehicle milestones to achieve, including success during Artemis III and flights afterward. This will all lead up to a key decision NASA must make: Which vehicle will carry out the first crewed landing on the surface of the moon since the Apollo program ended in 1972? Starship reached for the first time on its most recent test flight, which occurred on Sept. 28 from SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas. NASA lists several other important goals for the vehicle to achieve in 2026, including (in the order listed during the IAC presentation) the first return and catch of the rocket's upgraded Version 3 (V3) booster at its launch pad; the first-ever return and catch of a Ship upper stage; the first Starship launch from one of SpaceX's launch pads still under construction on Florida's Space Coast; and, possibly, the first V3 booster reflight. NASA also expects SpaceX to complete the initial build of the crew cabin for its lunar lander Starship variant. SpaceX released renders of Starship's interior last year , as well as images of the test elevator astronauts are using to train for Starship egress on the lunar surface, but little else has been made public about the progress the company has made on the cabin's design. Artist's rendering of the cabin of SpaceX's Starship vehicle during an Artemis moon mission for NASA. (Image credit: SpaceX) Should the cabin's initial build wrap up by the end of the year, as NASA's presentation suggested, SpaceX will use Q1 2027 to complete integration of the systems that Starship will need to communicate with Orion during Artemis III, and deliver a cabin simulator for astronauts to train on leading up to the mission. SpaceX plans to continue Starship test flights through Q2 of next year, complete a landing leg demonstration and begin crew cabin airlock tests. Blue Origin's lunar lander mockup is ready for NASA Artemis astronaut training For Artemis III, SpaceX plans to fly one of its existing V3 Starship upper stages, with some slight modifications. Starship and Orion will dock as part of Artemis III but the SpaceX vehicle won't be equipped with a crew cabin for the mission's astronauts to enter. Between the end of this year and the beginning of the next, SpaceX is expected to complete the addition of a docking system and nosecone cover to the Artemis III Starship vehicle, which, NASA documents suggest, has already completed its mechanical fit checks. Render of SpaceX Starship and Orion docked in low Earth orbit. (Image credit: SpaceX) Other notches on SpaceX's checklist leading up to Artemis III include the first propellant transfer demonstration with Starship in orbit. As the first-ever launch vehicle and spacecraft designed for full reusability, Starship's fuel constraints require that its tanks be topped off in order to fly beyond LEO. For a moon landing mission, this could mean up to a dozen launches of SpaceX's Starship "tanker" spacecraft to an orbiting fuel depot, which the moon-bound Starship will visit. To pull that off, though, SpaceX has to show it can successfully transfer those cryogenic fuels on orbit, and also store them effectively enough to prevent too much boil-off. Starship won't require any refueling flights to complete its objectives for Artemis III, but SpaceX is expected to launch its first Starship tanker vehicle within a few months of that mission as it gears up for the Artemis IV moon landing mission. To that end, a launch of an uncrewed Starship lunar lander variant is targeted sometime toward the end of Q3/beginning of Q4, with an uncrewed lunar landing mission carried out before the end of 2027. Blue Origin, meanwhile, has its own set of milestones to meet as it develops its Blue Moon Mark 2 (MK2) lander — a 52-foot-tall (16 meters) spacecraft powered by three BE-7 engines. Unlike the bare-bones V3 Starship that SpaceX will launch on Artemis III, Blue Origin plans to fly a completed test vehicle, incorporating the crew cabin, partial life-support, flight software and other systems needed to allow astronauts to enter the lander from Orion during their time docked in LEO. Astronauts will be able to enter Blue Moon from Orion to get a feel for the lander in zero-g and test some of its systems. Render of Blue Origin's Blue Moon lander and Orion prior to docking in low Earth orbit. (Image credit: Blue Moon) NASA's timeline shows the company working to complete a series of manufacturing and testing milestones in the last few months of 2026, including continued BE-7 testing and qualification of Blue Moon's BT-7 maneuvering thrusters. The company also faces its Artemis III interim design review and a critical design review for an upcoming landing demonstration mission in 2028. Blue Origin is also working to restore its pad at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station's Launch Complex-36 (LC-36) to operation and return its New Glenn rocket to flight, following an explosion of the rocket in May that caused extensive damage to the facility. NASA's presentation places that milestone in Q4 2026, a timeline the company has also been very vocal about maintaining. A recent Reuters report , however, suggests that may not happen until early 2027. By early 2027, the company expects to complete the spacecraft's communications systems and finalize its flight software, with assembly, integration and testing continuing into Q2. Q1 2027 is also when Blue Origin's Blue Moon MK1 lander (a smaller, uncrewed version of its MK2 successor) will launch to the lunar surface as a part of NASA's Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) program of robotic moon missions. A post shared by Space.com (@spacedotcom) A photo posted by During Q2 2027, as the Artemis III mission approaches, Blue Origin is expected to complete integration of its test lander with New Glenn and conclude qualification of it

item.title: 2026 AMAA Nominations: Slum Bomber, One Woman, One Bra & To Adaego With Love Lead the Pack
item.description: To Adaego With Love leads Nigerian nominations for the 2026 Africa Movie Academy Awards. Photo Credit: Nwamaka Chikezie/Instagram The nominations for the 22nd Africa Movie Academy Awards (AMAA) are out, and there’s already plenty to unpack ahead of the ceremony in Lagos this November. From Uganda and Kenya to Nigeria and South Africa, films from across the continent are competing for some of African cinema’s biggest honours. Leading this year’s nominations are Uganda’s Slum Bomber and Kenya’s One Woman , One Bra , with 14 nominations each. Nigeria is also well represented, with Nwamaka Chikezie ‘s To Adaego With Love earning 11 nominations, while Daniel Etim-Effiong ‘s The Herd follows closely with 10. They’re in good company. South Africa’s The Trek and Ben Made It , alongside Côte d’Ivoire’s Colours of Exile , have also received 10 nominations each, while Colours of Fire has nine. The nominees were announced during a livestream on AMAA’s official YouTube channel. Now, attention turns to the awards ceremony on 15 November 2026 at the Lagos Marriott Hotel, where filmmakers, actors and other industry professionals will gather to celebrate the year’s achievements in African cinema.
